# CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE BASE: FETAL ULTRASOUND SCREENING & CARDIAC ANATOMY
Source: ISUOG Practice Guidelines (Carvalho 2023) and Multi-Institutional Ultrasound Archive.

---

## 1. STANDARD ULTRASOUND VIEWS & ANATOMICAL PLANES

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Structures**: ascending aorta, descending aorta, main pulmonary artery
- **Acquisition**: Starting axial plane for cephalad arch sweep
- **Abnormal Quality Clue**: Assess separation of ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a gap between the ascending aorta and the main pulmonary artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Aortic arch
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: Targeted for visualization in the early fetal study.
- **Expected Anatomy**: A longitudinal fetal view demonstrates the aortic arch; used with four-chamber and outflow views in early assessment.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Optimal time for successful imaging of the four chambers and great arteries in early gestation appears to be between 13 to 14 weeks."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]; Jan Michael Smrcek et al. (2006), *Early Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Long-axis ventricular views
 - **Modality**: fetal B-mode ultrasound
- **Required Structure**: Left and right ventricles and their interventricular septum
- **Diagnostic Use**: Modified four-chamber and LV long-axis views are needed for perimembranous subaortic defects
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the detection of perimembranous subaortic defects can only be achieved by visualization of the modified four-chamber view and long-axis view of the left ventricle."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Right ventricular outflow tract or three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional gray-scale fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 21–23 weeks in this study
- **Quality**: The submitted RVOT or 3VV was scored for clarity of demonstration.
- **Illustrative Structures**: The 3VV example shows pulmonary artery, aorta and SVC with relative size and position.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Clear and well demonstrated"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. Sairam et al. (2009), *Impact of audit of routine second‐trimester cardiac images using a novel image‐scoring method* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Required Structures**: heart size, heart position in thorax, atrial symmetry, ventricular symmetry, atrioventricular valves, crux
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"assessment of the four-chamber view (size of the heart and position in thorax, symmetry of the atria and ventricles, identification of atrioventricular valves and crux)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Short-axis outflow tract view with septum tangential to beam
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Acquisition Context**: Group-I interventricular septum is tangential to the insonating beam.
- **Required Structures**: Both atria, right ventricle, tricuspid valve, pulmonary outflow and bifurcation, and aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"interventricular septum was tangential to the ultrasound beam"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Fetal sagittal retrocardiac view
- **Acquisition**: A sagittal retrocardiac view can reveal an infracardiac pulmonary venous collector crossing the diaphragm.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"collecteur veineux pulmonaire qui traverse le diaphragme"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber ventricular measurement plane
 - **Modality**: 2D cross-sectional fetal ultrasound
- **Required Structure**: Right and left ventricular diameters at the mitral and tricuspid valve level
- **Acquisition**: Measure ventricular diameters in diastole, inner myocardial edge to inner septal edge
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Ventricles were measured from the inner edge of the myocardial wall to the inner edge of the septal wall"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Kirk et al. (1999), *Fetal cardiac asymmetry: a marker for congenital heart disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Origin and crossover of great arteries
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: Targeted for visualization in the early fetal study.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"origin and crossover of the great arteries"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Jan Michael Smrcek et al. (2006), *Early Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] High transverse aortic-arch plane
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Appearance**: Only the left aortic arch is seen as a sausage-like structure on the left of the trachea
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Only the aortic arch is seen as a sausage-like structure"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Cephalad cross-sectional sweep from three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: 2D gray-scale fetal echocardiography, optionally color Doppler
- **Acquisition**: Sweep toward fetal head from 3VV to inspect both arches and any vessel coursing behind the trachea.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"straight back to the left of the midline and trachea"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Right ventricular outflow tract level
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Acquisition Or Assessment**: Intervening RVOT level may show two arterial signals in the illustrated conotruncal case.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) between the 4-chamber and 3-vessel and trachea views showed 2 arterial signals"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Required Structures**: The example shows right and left atria and ventricles; the paper recommends examining this view as part of screening and incorporating cardiac axis.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Normal four-chamber view. LA, left atrium; LV, left ventricle; RA, right atrium; RV, right ventricle."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. Small et al. (2004), *Indications for Fetal Echocardiography* [Pediatric Cardiology]

### [VIEW] Aortic wedge transverse plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Aorta between the two atria; ventricles foreshortened anterior to aorta.
- **Acquisition**: Transverse anatomical plane at the manubriosternal junction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the aorta wedged between the right and left atria"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Aortic outflow tract view with septum perpendicular to beam
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Acquisition Context**: Group-II interventricular septum is perpendicular to the beam.
- **Expected Anatomy**: Aorta exits left ventricle and arches with cephalad brachiocephalic and common carotid branches.
- **Expected Relationship**: Right pulmonary artery is perpendicular to the aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aortic outflow tract could be observed leaving the left ventricle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] First-trimester three vessels and trachea view with Doppler
 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Target a 3VT cross-section with color and/or directional power Doppler in CRL 45–84 mm fetuses.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"targeted cross-sections of the four-chamber view (4CV) and of the three vessels and trachea (3VT) view, using color and/or directional power Doppler"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Quarello et al. (2017), *Basic heart examination: feasibility study of first-trimester systematic simplified fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Great-artery origins and crossing
 - **Modality**: transvaginal echocardiography
- **Acquisition Target**: The early transvaginal protocol included visualizing the origin and crossing of the great arteries.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"origin and crossing of the great arteries"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. A. Rustico et al. (2000), *Early screening for fetal cardiac anomalies by transvaginal echocardiography in an unselected population: the role of operator experience* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Early fetal cardiac screening views
- **Criterion**: In detailed early screening, assess situs and cardiac axis.
- **Criterion**: In detailed early screening, obtain the four-chamber view with grayscale and color or bidirectional power Doppler.
- **Criterion**: In detailed early screening, use 3VTV to demonstrate the left-sided arches.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Situs, determined on grayscale imaging"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Upper abdominal and atrial situs planes
 - **Modality**: 2D and color Doppler fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Transverse upper abdominal and atrial views
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"leading to left-sided atrium (right atrium) (b)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Ductus arteriosus
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: Targeted for visualization in the early fetal study.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ductus arteriosus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Jan Michael Smrcek et al. (2006), *Early Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Specialist fetal echocardiography assessment
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 10–23 weeks at initial scan
- **Structures Assessed**: Heart position, four-chamber view, outflow tracts, and venous return
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"included assessment of the position of the heart, the four-chamber view, the outflow tracts and venous return"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Ghi et al. (2001), *Incidence of major structural cardiac defects associated with increased nuchal translucency but normal karyotype* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Oblique coronal fetal thorax view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Corrective Use**: Long-axis visualization of great vessels when prone fetal position shadows the transverse view.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"prone or semiprone ... difficult ... shadowing from the fetal scapula or spine ... oblique coronal plane"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel and trachea view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Structures**: trachea, aortic arch, ductus arteriosus, descending aorta
- **Normal Appearance**: Left aortic and ductal arches converge in a V- or Y-shape at the descending aorta beside the distal trachea
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"both the aortic arch and left ductus arteriosus are visualized forming a ‘V’-shaped confluence"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal outflow tract views
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Screening Role**: Outflow tract evaluation was used in the protocol and Table 4 to identify some abnormal cardiac appearances.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"either the 4-chamber view, outflow tracts, or in some cases both"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Karen M. Letourneau et al. (2018), *Advancing Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Disease: A Novel Screening Protocol Improves Early Diagnosis of Complex Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: Targeted for visualization in the early fetal study.
- **Acquisition Or Assessment**: Use an intervening axial three-vessel level when one oblique vessel prompts suspected transposition.
- **Sequence**: Part of the gray-scale examination before color flow mapping
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"3-vessel view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]; Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Slightly anterior pulmonary-vein plane
- **Acquisition**: A slightly more anterior plane near the aortic outflow tract displays the superior pulmonary veins.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"coupe un peu plus antérieure proche de la voie d’éjection aortique ... veines pulmonaires supérieures"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [VIEW] Fetal right outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Screening Use**: required in this historical protocol
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"and the right and left outflow tract views"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal longitudinal venae cavae drainage view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Study View Definition**: Core study view showing venae cavae drainage into right atrium
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view, right and left outflow tracts, transverse view of the ductus arteriosus and longitudinal view of the venae cavae drainage in the right atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2004), *The role of tissue harmonic imaging in fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Upper axial mediastinal three-vessel and trachea view
 - **Modality**: prenatal ultrasound
- **Acquisition Plane**: Axial view of upper fetal mediastinum with great vessels and tracheal location
- **Quality Criterion**: Identify the trachea relative to the ductal-aortic junction
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"axial view of the upper fetal mediastinum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] First-trimester general ultrasound cardiac check
 - **Modality**: first-trimester fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 10+0–13+6 general ultrasound in Figure S1
- **Heart Check**: pulse presence/absence, no measurement
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Heart pulse +/- (no measurement)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Hautala et al. (2019), *The implementation of a nationwide anomaly screening programme improves prenatal detection of major cardiac defects: an 11‐year national population‐based cohort study* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Pulmonary artery / right ventricular outflow view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: Main pulmonary artery bifurcation and pulmonary artery continuing into ductus arteriosus are shown in Figure 1.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Longitudinal view of pulmonary artery (PA) as it leads into ductus arteriosus (DU)."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Superior and inferior venae cavae
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: Targeted for visualization in the early fetal study.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"superior and inferior venae cavae"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Jan Michael Smrcek et al. (2006), *Early Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber transverse plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Four cardiac chambers with right ventricle anterior to left and atrioventricular valves visible.
- **Acquisition**: Transverse plane at the sternum–fifth costal cartilage junction in anatomical specimen.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The right ventricle is seen anterior to the left ventricle, and its thinner wall and coarser trabecular pattern are often distinguishable."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] First-trimester four-chamber view with Doppler
 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Target a 4CV cross-section with color and/or directional power Doppler in CRL 45–84 mm fetuses.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"targeted cross-sections of the four-chamber view (4CV) and of the three vessels and trachea (3VT) view, using color and/or directional power Doppler"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Quarello et al. (2017), *Basic heart examination: feasibility study of first-trimester systematic simplified fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber screening view
 - **Modality**: second-trimester fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 18–22 weeks in article; 18+0–21+6 in Fig S1
- **Required Assessments**: situs, axis, chamber size, chamber symmetry, heart rate, atrioventricular valves
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view (situs, axis, size and symmetry of the chambers, heart rate, av-valves)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Hautala et al. (2019), *The implementation of a nationwide anomaly screening programme improves prenatal detection of major cardiac defects: an 11‐year national population‐based cohort study* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Foramen ovale colour-flow assessment
 - **Modality**: colour-flow Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Functional Criterion**: Predominant right-to-left shunting is described as the usual fetal pattern.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"normal shunting across the foramen ovale is predominantly right to left in fetal life"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Fetal three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Acquisition Plane**: Transverse plane cranial to the four-chamber view
- **Expected Structures**: Pulmonary artery/ductus arteriosus, transverse aorta, and superior caval vein
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"This plane consists of the pulmonary artery/ductus arteriosus, with a transverse section through the aorta and superior caval vein"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Sheila M.P. Everwijn et al. (2018), *The effect of the introduction of the three‐vessel view on the detection rate of transposition of the great arteries and tetralogy of Fallot* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view: pulmonary venous entry
- **Expected Anatomy**: Assess the left venoatrial junction and pulmonary venous drainage into the left atrium in the four-chamber view.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"assessment of the left venoatrial junction is part of the four-chamber-view evaluation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition Plane**: transverse fetal thorax just above four-chamber view
- **Expected Anatomy**: aorta, pulmonary artery, spatial relationship
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"three-vessel view (a transverse section of the fetal thorax, just above the level of the four-chamber view)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber fetal heart view
 - **Modality**: transvaginal echocardiography
- **Acquisition Target**: At 13–15 weeks, the protocol attempted the four-chamber view and great-artery origin and crossing for each fetus.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view and the origin and crossing of the great arteries"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. A. Rustico et al. (2000), *Early screening for fetal cardiac anomalies by transvaginal echocardiography in an unselected population: the role of operator experience* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Plane posterior to four-chamber view
- **Acquisition**: A plane posterior to the four-chamber view can show coronary sinus dilation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"coupe postérieure à la coupe des 4 cavités, le sinus coronaire apparaît dilaté"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [VIEW] Long-axis aortic outflow view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: Aortic outflow from left ventricular region in Figure 1C.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Normal long-axis view of heart showing aortic outflow tract"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view
- **Criterion**: Confirm two atria and two ventricles in the four-chamber plane.
- **Criterion**: Examine the cardiac crux and atrioventricular junction.
- **Criterion**: Inspect the ventricular septum from apex to crux.
- **Required Details**: Image quality assessed by heart magnification, AV valve offset, and interventricular septum from apex to crux.
- **Screening Role**: Used in the protocol and Table 4 to identify some abnormal cardiac appearances.
- **Supports Measurement**: The transverse fetal chest view at the cardiac four-chamber level permits cardiac axis and position assessment in this study.
- **Used In Screening**: Referring first-line sonographers used the standard four-chamber view along with a great-vessel view.
- **Expected Anatomy**: Two atria and two ventricles of equal size in this study checklist.
- **Required Structures**: Moderator band in anterior right ventricle, tricuspid valve closer to apex than mitral valve, and intact ventricular septum.
- **Depicted Structures**: Left and right atria and ventricles; mitral and tricuspid valves are annotated in Figure panel a
- **Study Acquisition**: Visualized first in the extended fetal echocardiographic examination
- **Screen Orientation**: When the heart is confirmed left-sided, display apex on screen left and base on screen right.
- **Diagnostic Limitation**: Outflow tract malformations may not alter the four-chamber appearance.
- **Limitation**: Can appear normal with outflow tract and great artery anomalies
- **Acquisition Quality**: Prefer a lateral rather than only apical projection for this rim assessment; ventricular wall more perpendicular to beam.
- **Required Structure**: Four cardiac chambers and septal orientation in a transverse fetal chest plane
- **Required Structure**: Assess the posterior left atrium and whether two pulmonary veins form a confluence with a broad opening into the left atrium.
- **Acquisition**: A strict four-chamber axial thoracic plane at the sixth intercostal space displays the inferior pulmonary veins.
- **Required Structures**: Left and right atria and ventricles are visible for side-to-side comparison.
- **Measurement Plane**: Maximal LV and RV widths measured below the atrioventricular valve orifice.
- **Limitation**: A normal-appearing four-chamber view can occur with listed conotruncal abnormalities.
- **Screening Limitation**: TGA and ToF generally can have a normal four-chamber appearance
- **Expected Anatomy**: The coronary sinus lies posterior to the left atrium/atrioventricular groove
- **Indirect Clue**: Unusually prominent coronary sinus may suggest PLSVC but is not specific
- **Acquisition**: Four-chamber view was among the views obtained during segmental cardiac screening.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Intact cardiac crux"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Isabelle Durand et al. (2022), *Outcomes following prenatal diagnosis of isolated persistent left superior vena cava* [Archives of Cardiovascular Diseases]; E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view with color Doppler
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound plus color Doppler
- **Proposed Additional View**: Authors propose considering a three-vessel view with color Doppler for outflow and great-artery anomalies.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"an incorporation of the three-vessel view with color Doppler might be considered"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal right outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Study View Definition**: Core study intrathoracic view; relates to assessment of ventriculo-arterial connections
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view, right and left outflow tracts, transverse view of the ductus arteriosus and longitudinal view of the venae cavae drainage in the right atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2004), *The role of tissue harmonic imaging in fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal atrioventricular inflow Doppler
 - **Modality**: spectral Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Assesses**: Mitral or tricuspid inflow pattern and duration in progressive outflow obstruction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a uniphasic rather than biphasic Doppler inflow pattern was observed"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [VIEW] Ventricular outflow tract views
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Screening Role**: Outflow tract views can demonstrate transposed great vessels and were considered necessary for antenatal TGA detection.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"TGA is detectable on antenatal ultrasound scanning, as long as the cardiac views include the outflow tracts"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Blyth et al. (2008), *The hidden mortality of transposition of the great arteries and survival advantage provided by prenatal diagnosis* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal great-vessel view
 - **Modality**: ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 18 weeks for proposed routine-screening emphasis
- **Used In Screening**: Great-vessel views were part of first-line screening where TGA was suspected.
- **Target Feature**: Parallel great vessels were the proposed feature to seek in routine screening at 18 weeks.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"standard 4-chamber view and the great-vessel view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Damien Bonnet et al. (1999), *Detection of Transposition of the Great Arteries in Fetuses Reduces Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Main pulmonary artery bifurcation view
- **Depicted Structures**: Main pulmonary artery and its bifurcation
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"main pulmonary artery and its bifurcation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (1992), *Extended fetal echocardiographic examination for detecting cardiac malformations in low risk pregnancies.* [BMJ]

### [VIEW] Long-axis venous drainage view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Required Structures**: Left SVC, coronary sinus and atrial drainage course
- **Confirmation Criterion**: Trace direct or indirect drainage via coronary sinus into an atrium
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"then confirmed in the long-axis view, demonstrating direct or indirect drainage via the coronary sinus into the left or right atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: A. Galindo et al. (2007), *Clinical significance of persistent left superior vena cava diagnosed in fetal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Aortic arch longitudinal plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Aortic arch into descending aorta, with ascending head/neck arteries and esophageal relation.
- **Acquisition**: Increase sagittal-plane angulation rather than following the ductus.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the aortic arch can be traced into the descending aorta. The head and neck arteries are seen ascending from the arch and the relation to the oesophagus is seen"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Fetal left outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Study View Definition**: Core study intrathoracic view; relates to assessment of ventriculo-arterial connections
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view, right and left outflow tracts, transverse view of the ductus arteriosus and longitudinal view of the venae cavae drainage in the right atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2004), *The role of tissue harmonic imaging in fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Color three-vessel-and-trachea view
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Acquisition Or Assessment**: Assess the arterial arms of the V sign, relative size, and flow direction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"number of arterial arms, subjective impression of their size ratio, and flow direction"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Left ventricular and aortic long-axis view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Used For**: Ascending aorta diameter above root in ventricular systole
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ascending aorta diameter above the aortic root, during ventricular systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber aortic-root plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Aortic root arising from left ventricle in four-chamber projection.
- **Acquisition**: Add cranial obliquity to the four-chamber transverse plane.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"By adding cranial obliquity to the transverse plane at the level of the fifth costal cartilage the aortic root is seen in four chamber projection originating from the left ventricle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Required Anatomy**: Main pulmonary artery, ascending aorta, superior vena cava, descending aorta and airway relations are assessed as source-described.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A cephalad cross-sectional sweep from the 3VV shows the normal leftward position of the aortic arch and ductus arteriosus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Coronal tracheal view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Expected Observation**: Coronal images can show vascular structures on either side of the trachea above the carina.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"2 vascular structures (the LAA and RAA) in a short-axis view on either side of the carina"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Left ventricular outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional gray-scale fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 21–23 weeks in this study
- **Required Details**: The audit checks demonstration of septoaortic continuity and the outflow tract arising from the LV.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Septoaortic continuity demonstrated clearly with outflow tract"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. Sairam et al. (2009), *Impact of audit of routine second‐trimester cardiac images using a novel image‐scoring method* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Transverse fetal abdominal and thoracic situs planes
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 20 weeks in this case
- **Acquisition**: Maternal transverse sections through fetal abdomen and thorax
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Maternal transverse sections show transverse sections through fetus’s abdominal (a) and thoracic regions (b)."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Sagittal aortic arch view
- **Criterion**: Sagittal aortic views are part of fetal echocardiography and may be included in screening under some local protocols.
- **Criterion**: The sagittal arch view can show the three aortic branches.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Sagittal views of aorta are part of fetal echocardiography"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Main pulmonary artery / pulmonary outflow tract
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Screening Target**: The main pulmonary artery or pulmonary outflow tract was a target for visualization when technically feasible.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the main pulmonary artery, aortic outflow tract, or both"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Ivana M. Vettraino et al. (2005), *Sonographic Evaluation of the Ventricular Cardiac Outflow Tracts* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Fetal aortic outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: 2D/color/CW Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Assesses**: Aortic valve morphology and forward flow by grayscale, color and spectral Doppler.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In milder AS, doming and mild thickening of the aortic valve may be observed. Color and pulsed Doppler interrogation of the aortic outflow tract usually reveals increased velocities with minimal gradient and often mild post-stenotic dilation of the ascending aorta."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [VIEW] Fetal axial abdominal vessel view
- **Required Structure**: Assess abnormal abdominal vessels, especially a collector in front of the aorta and inferior vena cava to the right of the stomach.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"vaisseau anormal (collecteur) en avant de l’aorte et la veine cave inférieure, à droite de l’estomac"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [VIEW] Left ventricular short-axis plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Left ventricle in short axis with RV infundibulum anterosuperior and pulmonary valve visible.
- **Acquisition**: Sagittal cut left of sternum with slight obliquity toward left shoulder.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the left ventricle is seen in its short axis with the right ventricular infundibulum ascending anterosuperiorly. The pulmonary valve is visualised in this plane"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Long-axis view of LSVC drainage
 - **Modality**: 2D and color Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Required Structure**: Track the left superior vena cava through the coronary sinus to the right atrium.
- **Color Doppler**: Color Doppler was used to demonstrate direct drainage.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"confirmed in long-axis view (Fig. 2), demonstrated by colour Doppler direct drainage via the coronary sinus into the right atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Isabelle Durand et al. (2022), *Outcomes following prenatal diagnosis of isolated persistent left superior vena cava* [Archives of Cardiovascular Diseases]

### [VIEW] Right ventricular outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: approximately 13–14 weeks
- **Expected Anatomy**: A longitudinal fetal view demonstrates the right ventricular outflow tract and pulmonary artery.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Optimal time for successful imaging of the four chambers and great arteries in early gestation appears to be between 13 to 14 weeks."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view and great-artery cross-over
 - **Modality**: transvaginal fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 11–14 weeks
- **Acquisition Target**: Early scans may assess pulmonary trunk, three-vessel view, and cross-over of the great arteries.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A 20% success rate was encountered at 11 weeks as opposed to 92% at 13 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [VIEW] Upper-mediastinal LBCV plane cranial to 3VT
 - **Modality**: transabdominal grayscale and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 18–24 weeks in prospective cohort
- **Acquisition Plane**: Sweep slightly cranial to the 3VT plane to depict the LBCV across the upper mediastinum.
- **Expected Anatomy**: Normal LBCV lies posterior to thymus, superior to aortic arch and anterior to its brachiocephalic branches, draining to SVC.
- **Quality Criterion**: Assess LBCV in both grayscale and color Doppler.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"crosses the upper mediastinum in an oblique plane anterior and superior to the aortic arch and posterior to the thymus gland"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2016), *Intrathymic and other anomalous courses of the left brachiocephalic vein in the fetus* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Oblique sagittal ductal-arch long-axis view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Align pulmonary trunk and descending aorta with the beam, then rotate about 90 degrees
- **Expected Appearance**: Hockey-stick ductal arch continuous with pulmonary artery and without head/neck branches
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the transducer is rotated 90◦"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Short-axis right ventricle and main pulmonary artery
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Study Acquisition**: Obtained after approximately 90-degree rotation of the probe
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the short axis of the right ventricle axis with the main pulmonary artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Fetal three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Plane**: Orthogonal transverse view of the fetal upper mediastinum
- **Required Structures**: main pulmonary artery, ascending aorta, superior vena cava
- **Normal Alignment**: The three vessels are aligned in a straight line.
- **Normal Size Order**: Main pulmonary artery, ascending aorta and superior vena cava decrease in size in that order.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"arranged in a straight line and sized in decreasing order"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [VIEW] Tricuspid-pulmonary longitudinal plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Pulmonary valve anterior and cranial to aortic root; right atrium and right ventricular inflow/outflow identified.
- **Acquisition**: Longitudinal fetal-axis plane, anatomical correlate approximately 20° oblique to coronal plane.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"cutting the abortus parallel to the spinal cord with about 20° obliquity to the coronal plane"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Left ventricular long-axis plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Aortic root from LV with aortic–mitral continuity and anterior RV infundibulum.
- **Acquisition**: Oblique transverse cut toward the fetal right shoulder.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"taking a transverse plane with some obliquity away from the horizontal towards the right shoulder"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Cardiac outflow tract screening views
 - **Modality**: second-trimester fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 18–22 weeks in article
- **Required Assessment**: great artery crossing
- **Required Structures**: RVOT, pulmonary trunk, LVOT, aorta
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"right ventricle outflow tract and pulmonary trunk, left ventricle outflow tract and aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Hautala et al. (2019), *The implementation of a nationwide anomaly screening programme improves prenatal detection of major cardiac defects: an 11‐year national population‐based cohort study* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal three-vessel view
- **Depicts**: Main pulmonary artery, ascending aorta, superior vena cava and branch pulmonary arteries.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Three-vessel view shows the main pulmonary artery (PA), ascending aorta (Ao), superior vena cava (SVC), and a hypoplastic RPA coursing behind the ascending aorta."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M M Abdullah et al. (2000), *Fetal cardiac dextroposition in the absence of an intrathoracic mass: sign of significant right lung hypoplasia.* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Oblique sagittal aortic-arch long-axis view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Align ascending and descending aorta with the beam in 3VV, then rotate transducer about 90 degrees
- **Expected Appearance**: Candy-cane arch rising centrally and giving off head and neck branches
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the transducer is rotated 90◦"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber M-mode plane for pericardial fluid
 - **Modality**: M-mode fetal echocardiography | **Gestational Age**: 19–38 weeks in study
- **Acquisition**: Align ventricular septum perpendicular to ultrasound beam in four-chamber plane for M-mode fluid assessment.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The pericardial fluid was evaluated by M-mode in the four-chamber plane in which the ventricular septum was aligned perpendicular to the ultrasound beam axis"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2001), *Normal pericardial fluid in the fetus: color and spectral Doppler analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Ventricular short-axis view
 - **Modality**: real-time obstetric ultrasound
- **Quality Criterion**: Show both ventricular walls and test whether the rim continues through the ventricular septum.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"whether it continued circumferentially through the ventricular septum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Douglas L. Brown et al. (1989), *The peripheral hypoechoic rim of the fetal heart* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel and trachea view with color Doppler
 - **Modality**: color Doppler ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 20–24 weeks in study
- **Acquisition**: Add color flow mapping to the 3VTV plane
- **Assessment**: Color Doppler permitted evaluation of flow direction
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"permitted to study the direction of flow"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]

### [VIEW] Right ventricular outflow tract view with color Doppler
 - **Modality**: grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 16–22 weeks in study
- **Acquisition**: Interrogate the ventricular outflow tract with grayscale and color Doppler.
- **Limitation**: Main pulmonary artery dilation may be subtle on grayscale despite color flow aliasing.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view and the ventricular outflow tracts"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Allan S. Nadel et al. (2010), *Addition of Color Doppler to the Routine Obstetric Sonographic Survey Aids in the Detection of Pulmonic Stenosis* [Fetal Diagnosis and Therapy]

### [VIEW] Longitudinal aortic and ductal arch views
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Aortic Arch**: Normal longitudinal aortic arch in Figure 1D.
- **Ductal Arch**: Pulmonary artery leading to ductus arteriosus in Figure 1E.
- **Acquisition**: Included when possible.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Aortic and ductal arches were included when possible"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Right atrial inlet and outlet long-axis view
- **Depicted Structures**: Inferior and superior vena cava joining the right atrial region
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"long axis view through inlet and outlet of right atrium showing inferior and superior vena cava"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (1992), *Extended fetal echocardiographic examination for detecting cardiac malformations in low risk pregnancies.* [BMJ]

### [VIEW] Fetal transverse abdominal situs view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Required Structures**: Spine, liver and stomach establish fetal laterality and visceral situs
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The major visceral landmarks available in fetal echocardiography are the liver and stomach."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [VIEW] Fetal aortic arch view
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography with Doppler
- **Assessed For**: Distal aortic arch flow direction
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"direction of ductus arteriosus and foramen ovale flow"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Sagittal fetal pulmonary outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: 2D/color/CW Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Assesses**: Pulmonary valve doming, main pulmonary artery and pulmonary outflow turbulence/gradient.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"turbulence observed at the level of the pulmonary valve"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel-and-trachea view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional transabdominal ultrasound
- **Used For**: Identify the fetal thymus in the upper mediastinum for TT-ratio measurement.
- **Expected Anatomy**: The source situates the thymus near the great vessels, transverse aortic arch, sternum, and vertebral body.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"between the anterior edge of the thoracic vertebral body posteriorly and the internal edge of the sternum anteriorly"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2012), *Thymic–thoracic ratio in fetuses with trisomy 21, 18 or 13* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional obstetric ultrasound
- **Acquisition Plane**: Transverse fetal thorax above the diaphragm
- **Heart To Thorax Area Qualitative**: ≤ one third of thorax
- **Normal Appearance**: two equal-sized atria
- **Normal Appearance**: two symmetric ventricles with equal contraction
- **Normal Appearance**: offset atrioventricular valve attachment at crux
- **Normal Appearance**: foramen ovale present
- **Normal Appearance**: apparently intact ventricular septum
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the foramen ovale defect is present in the atrial septum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: GURLEEN K. SHARLAND et al. (1992), *Screening for congenital heart disease prenatally. Results of a 2½‐year study in the South East Thames Region* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Right ventricular outflow-tract view
- **Criterion**: Show pulmonary artery origin from the morphological right ventricle.
- **Criterion**: Show main pulmonary artery bifurcation after a short course.
- **Depicted Structures**: Right ventricular outflow tract
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"branching after a short course"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]; R. Achiron et al. (1992), *Extended fetal echocardiographic examination for detecting cardiac malformations in low risk pregnancies.* [BMJ]

### [VIEW] Fetal cardiac outflow tract views
 - **Modality**: obstetric screening ultrasound
- **Screening Utility**: Outflow tract views are described as needed to detect TGA, TOF and double-outlet right ventricle.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"defects such as TGA, TOF, and double-outlet right ventricle, which require OFTVs for diagnosis"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Michael D. Quartermain et al. (2015), *Variation in Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease in Infants* [Pediatrics]

### [VIEW] Fetal pulmonary venous Doppler
 - **Modality**: spectral Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Assesses**: Early diastolic forward pulmonary venous flow and atrial-systolic reversal as left atrial pressure changes.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Severe left atrial hypertension is associated with little or no forward flow from the pulmonary veins into the left atrium during early ventricular diastole and increasing volume of reversed flow during atrial systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [VIEW] Main pulmonary artery short-axis view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Used For**: Main pulmonary artery diameter in ventricular systole
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"main pulmonary artery diameter midway between the pulmonary valve and the bifurcation, also during ventricular systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Slanted coronal tracheal-bifurcation view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Required Structures**: trachea, right main bronchus, left main bronchus, aortic arch, ductal arch
- **Normal Appearance**: Both aortic and ductal arches are left of the trachea in the source's normal example
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Both aortic arch (AA) and ductal arch are seen on the left side of the trachea"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber fetal screening view
 - **Modality**: obstetric screening ultrasound
- **Study Classifies Likely Normal**: TGA, TOF, DORV, truncus arteriosus
- **Study Classifies Likely Abnormal**: complete AVSD, congenitally corrected TGA, tricuspid valve disease, single-ventricle defects including HLHS
- **Classification Limitation**: Other diagnoses can have variable four-chamber appearance by severity or gestational age.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"normal 4CV included transposition of the great arteries (TGA), tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), double-outlet right ventricle, and truncus arteriosus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Michael D. Quartermain et al. (2015), *Variation in Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease in Infants* [Pediatrics]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber color Doppler plane for pericardial fluid
 - **Modality**: color Doppler fetal echocardiography | **Gestational Age**: 19–38 weeks in study
- **Acquisition**: Align ventricular septum approximately parallel to beam for color Doppler evaluation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"For Doppler evaluation, the ventricular septum was aligned as parallel as possible with the ultrasound beam axis."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2001), *Normal pericardial fluid in the fetus: color and spectral Doppler analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Longitudinal fetal aortic-arch view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Required Structure**: Aortic arch and descending aorta in longitudinal projection.
- **Limitation**: Normal appearance does not exclude coarctation in this study.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"arch appears normal in this view even though this fetus had a coarctation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Left ventricular outflow-tract view
- **Criterion**: Show the first great vessel arising from the morphological left ventricle.
- **Criterion**: Document septoaortic continuity in the LVOT plane.
- **Depicted Structures**: Left ventricular outflow tract and root of ascending aorta
- **Study Acquisition**: Obtained after approximately 90-degree rotation of the probe
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Continuity should be documented between the ventricular septum and the anterior wall"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]; J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Ventricular outflow tracts
 - **Modality**: fetal B-mode ultrasound
- **Required Structures**: Left and right ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries
- **Limitation**: Isolated subarterial outlet VSDs need outflow-tract and LV long-axis examination
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"isolated subarterial outlet VSDs, whose diagnosis require the examination of the ventricular outflow tracts and a long-axis view of the left ventricle."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Short-axis-guided ventricular M-mode
 - **Modality**: M-mode fetal echocardiography
- **Quality Criterion**: Cursor within approximately 15° of perpendicular to myocardial tangent for descriptive measurement.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"measured unless the M-mode cursor line could be positioned within approximately a 15° angle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Douglas L. Brown et al. (1989), *The peripheral hypoechoic rim of the fetal heart* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Fetal sagittal orientation view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Required Orientation**: Fetal head is displayed on the right before transverse rotation
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The fetal head and sagittal plane of fetal body are then located. The transducer is oriented so that it is parallel to the fetal sagittal plane, with the fetal head on the right side of the video screen (Figure 1)."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [VIEW] Outflow tract views
 - **Modality**: midgestation fetal ultrasound
- **Required Structures In Study Definition**: Aortic and pulmonary valves with crossing great arteries
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"OFTVs (aortic/pulmonary valves with crossing great arteries)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Simultaneous pulsed-wave Doppler atrial–ventricular trace
 - **Modality**: pulsed-wave Doppler
- **Acquisition**: Record atrial and ventricular flow markers simultaneously, including LV inflow–outflow or pulmonary artery/vein sampling.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"at 30 (a) ... weeks of gestation, showing sinus bradycardia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Ventricular short-axis view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Used For**: End-diastolic ventricular short-axis diameters just below AV valve
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"end-diastolic left ventricular and right ventricular diameters measured just below the atrioventricular valve from a short-axis view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Ductus longitudinal plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Pulmonary trunk curves posteriorly through ductus arteriosus to descending aorta.
- **Acquisition**: From tricuspid-pulmonary plane, change beam obliquity to follow pulmonary trunk posteriorly.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the pulmonary trunk can be shown sweeping posteriorly and connecting via the ductus arteriosus with the descending aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Aortic arch and ductus
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Study Acquisition**: Visualized after approximately 90-degree rotation of the probe
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"and the aortic arch and ductus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view with descending-aorta position
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Assessment**: Assess descending-aorta position relative to left atrium, pulmonary veins and spine when evaluating a ring.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In 8 of the 9 cases, the descending aorta coursed more centrally rather than to the left in front of the fetal spine"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber screening view with color Doppler
 - **Modality**: grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 16–22 weeks in study
- **Acquisition**: Use grayscale four-chamber imaging and activate color Doppler to inspect valve flow.
- **Limitation**: Right atrial enlargement can be unapparent on the screening grayscale image.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"normal antegrade flow through all 4 cardiac valves"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Allan S. Nadel et al. (2010), *Addition of Color Doppler to the Routine Obstetric Sonographic Survey Aids in the Detection of Pulmonic Stenosis* [Fetal Diagnosis and Therapy]

### [VIEW] Short-axis great-vessel view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Abnormal Examples**: VSD with overriding aorta and parallel great vessels are illustrated.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Short-axis view of same fetus showing large ventricular septal defect (VSD) with large overriding aorta (AO)."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: midgestation fetal ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: Left and right ventricles are displayed in Figure 1A at 30 weeks.
- **Illustrative Appearance**: One affected case had no obvious four-chamber abnormality at approximately 22 weeks.
- **Depicts**: Heart position and ventricular septal axis relative to the thoracic midline.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Four-chamber view (4-CV) without obvious abnormality at approximately 22 weeks’ gestation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]; L. R. Freud et al. (2015), *Low rate of prenatal diagnosis among neonates with critical aortic stenosis: insight into the natural history in utero* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Distal aortic arch flow assessment
 - **Modality**: color Doppler fetal echocardiography
- **Assesses**: Antegrade versus retrograde distal aortic arch flow during critical aortic obstruction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Retrograde aortic arch flow confirms the presence of critical AS in which LV output is insufficient to drive forward flow through the distal arch"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel and trachea view
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Relation To Lbcv Plane**: The dedicated LBCV plane is slightly cranial to 3VT; the retrotracheal example was imaged at 3VT level.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In a slightly cephalad plane to the 3VT view, the left brachiocephalic vein (LBCV), or innominate vein, can be seen."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2016), *Intrathymic and other anomalous courses of the left brachiocephalic vein in the fetus* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel-and-trachea view
- **Criterion**: Show ductal and aortic arches left of the trachea, converging toward the descending aorta.
- **Criterion**: The plane may need slight obliquity or transducer adjustment to show both arches.
- **Acquisition**: Move the probe cephalad from the four-chamber plane
- **Structures**: The source labels superior vena cava or cava vein, aorta, main pulmonary artery and trachea
- **Assessment**: Identify vessel number, gross vessel size, and vessel relationship to the trachea
- **Required Structure**: Look for a fourth vessel to the left of the pulmonary artery and compare the right superior vena cava caliber.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"slightly oblique transverse plane"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]; J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Upper-mediastinal three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Required Structures**: Pulmonary trunk/artery, ascending aorta, arterial duct and RSVC relationship in the upper mediastinum
- **Abnormal Plsvc Appearance**: Fourth vessel to the left of the pulmonary trunk and arterial duct when both SVCs are present
- **Absent Rsvc Variant**: Three vessels can remain but in abnormal right-to-left aorta–pulmonary artery–PLSVC order
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Figure 1 Abnormal three-vessel view at 20 weeks showing a supernumerary vessel left of the pulmonary trunk and arterial duct (AD). AAo, ascending aorta; LSVC, left superior vena cava; PA, pulmonary artery; RSVC, right superior vena cava; T, trachea."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: A. Galindo et al. (2007), *Clinical significance of persistent left superior vena cava diagnosed in fetal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Subcostal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: fetal B-mode ultrasound
- **Quality Criterion**: Confirm a suspected VSD in at least two planes because the apical four-chamber view may show artifactual hypoechogenicity
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Because of artifactual areas of hypoechogenicity in the apical four-chamber view, a true VSD is confirmed only when it is visible in at least two different planes."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal left outflow tract view
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Screening Use**: required in this historical protocol
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"and the right and left outflow tract views"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [VIEW] Aortic outflow tract
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Screening Target**: The aortic outflow tract was a target for visualization when technically feasible.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the main pulmonary artery, aortic outflow tract, or both"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Ivana M. Vettraino et al. (2005), *Sonographic Evaluation of the Ventricular Cardiac Outflow Tracts* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Five-chamber view
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Acquisition Or Assessment**: The illustrated 5-chamber level shows one large overriding vessel with turbulent flow.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"1 large overriding vessel with turbulent flow is shown at the level of the 5-chamber view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: Heart/chest and chamber measurements were made from this plane.
- **Acquisition Or Assessment**: Assess two ventricular inflow stripes, their relative size, and septal separation.
- **Acquisition Scope**: Routine second-trimester ultrasound; Phase II tried to obtain the four-chamber view in every fetus
- **Expected Anatomy**: At 13 weeks the normal transverse chest section demonstrates four chambers with RA, RV, LA and LV; assess symmetry and atrioventricular junction.
- **Quality Criterion**: Show situs, connections, AV junction, right-left symmetry and septoaortic continuity; document limitations.
- **Used For**: Left and right ventricular long-axis and atrioventricular annulus measurements
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"to demonstrate ‘normality’ of situs and cardiac connections"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]; E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Great-artery measurement plane
 - **Modality**: 2D cross-sectional fetal ultrasound
- **Required Structure**: Aorta and pulmonary artery at their valve levels
- **Acquisition**: Measure diameters between inner vessel-wall edges
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The great arteries were measured at the level of the aortic and pulmonic valves"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Kirk et al. (1999), *Fetal cardiac asymmetry: a marker for congenital heart disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view
- **Criterion**: Assess vessel number, relative size, alignment, and arrangement in the three-vessel view.
- **Criterion**: Expect pulmonary artery, aorta, and right superior vena cava from left to right.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"From left to right, the vessels are the pulmonary artery, aorta and right superior vena cava"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Basal short-axis sweep
 - **Modality**: fetal B-mode ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Apex-to-base sweep along the short axis to inspect septal continuity
- **Sequence**: Basal short-axis follows four-chamber and outflow-tract assessment in this study
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"an apex-to-base sweep along the short axis of the heart"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Aortic valve flow assessment
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography and Doppler
- **Measurement Timing**: Semilunar valves, including the aortic valve, were measured during systole in this study.
- **Observed Features**: Valve thickening/dysplasia and mild flow acceleration were described at mid-gestation in the selected cases.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Atrioventricular valves and ventricular dimensions were measured at end-diastole and semilunar valves were measured during systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: L. R. Freud et al. (2015), *Low rate of prenatal diagnosis among neonates with critical aortic stenosis: insight into the natural history in utero* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Four-chamber view for descending-aorta position
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Arch Anomaly Check**: Observe whether descending aorta lies right or midline relative to spine
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"descending aorta is seen on the right side or in the midline"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Three-vessel view of fetal upper mediastinum
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional transabdominal fetal ultrasound
- **Expected Anatomy**: Main pulmonary artery, ascending aorta, and superior vena cava in a left-anterior to right-posterior line with decreasing size.
- **Adequacy**: Round aortic and SVC cross-sections and an oblique main pulmonary artery section.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"round cross-sections of the ascending aorta and superior vena cava and an oblique section of the main pulmonary artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Study View Definition**: Core study view; source images and captions show atria, ventricles, atrioventricular junction and ventricular volumes
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"both images are adequate to assess atria and ventricles, but the THI image (left) is clearer"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2004), *The role of tissue harmonic imaging in fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal four-chamber screening view
 - **Modality**: prenatal ultrasound
- **Screening Role**: Routine obstetric cardiac screening plane described by the authors
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"standard ‘4-chamber cardiac view’ used by obstetricians for screening"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Wayne Tworetzky et al. (2001), *Improved Surgical Outcome After Fetal Diagnosis of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Standardized fetal transverse thoracic view
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Expected Orientation**: After 90-degree clockwise transducer rotation, image is presented caudal-to-cranial
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The fetal transverse image thus acquired is presented in the caudal-to-cranial perspective."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [VIEW] Longitudinal fetal ventriculoarterial views
 - **Modality**: 2D and color Doppler fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Longitudinal views demonstrate the arterial origins and relative artery positions
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Pulmonary artery, posterior to aorta, and duct (arrow) are also identified (b, c)."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Fetal great-artery views
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional obstetric ultrasound
- **Required Structures**: Crossing ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery; aortic arch and ductal arch.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"crossing of the ascending aorta with main pulmonary artery; aortic arch and ductal arch"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Acquisition Plane**: Transverse section of fetal thorax just above diaphragm, assessed during routine scan around 18 weeks
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"transverse section of the fetal thorax, just above the diaphragm"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1994), *Incorporating the four‐chamber view of the fetal heart into the second‐trimester routine fetal examination* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal cardiac four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: ultrasound
- **Associated Assessments**: The same heart checklist assessed size and rhythm.
- **Acquisition**: Used for retrospective cardiac-axis measurement and for evaluating chamber appearance and symmetry.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"draw a line from the spine to the anterior chest wall ... measure the angle formed between the intraventricular septum and this bisecting line"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Thomas D. Shipp et al. (1995), *Levorotation of the Fetal Cardiac Axis: A Clue for the Presence of Congenital Heart Disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]; P. Schwärzler et al. (1999), *Feasibility of the second‐trimester fetal ultrasound examination in an unselected population at 18, 20 or 22 weeks of pregnancy: a randomized trial* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Upper abdominal situs view
- **Criterion**: Establish fetal right and left before assessing abdominal and cardiac situs.
- **Criterion**: The axial upper-abdominal view should show the stomach on the fetal left.
- **Criterion**: Assess the descending aorta left of the spine and inferior vena cava right of the spine.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"stomach visible on the left side"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Sagittal chest plane for double LBCV
 - **Modality**: grayscale fetal ultrasound
- **Demonstrated Structures**: Two vessels were seen anterior to the aorta in the illustrated double-LBCV case.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In the sagittal plane (c), two vessels are seen anterior to the aorta (Ao). The finding of a double LBCV was an incidental one in this fetus."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2016), *Intrathymic and other anomalous courses of the left brachiocephalic vein in the fetus* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Right-sided fetal four-chamber plane
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Transverse thoracic four-chamber view in a fetus with right-sided heart
