- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Transverse section through fetus’s chest shows right-sided four-chamber view."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [VIEW] Fetal M-mode atrial–ventricular timing trace
 - **Modality**: M-mode echocardiography
- **Acquisition**: Record atrial and ventricular wall motion simultaneously to compare A–A, V–V and AV intervals.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A-A intervals (expressed in ms) be measured accurately ... Five to 10 cardiac cycles are usually sufficient"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [VIEW] Fetal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Assesses**: Relative chamber size, ventricular function, and atrioventricular valve consequences in evolving outflow obstruction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"At 16 weeks, the four-chamber view demonstrated a dilated RV with poor systolic function"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [VIEW] Transverse fetal aortic-arch and duct comparison
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Expected Anatomy**: The arch and duct should appear similar in size in the authors’ transverse comparison.
- **Acquisition**: Compare arch with pulmonary artery and duct in a transverse fetal thorax section.
- **Abnormal Appearance**: A hypoplastic arch relative to duct is shown in proven coarctation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aortic arch is hypoplastic and the pulmonary artery and duct appear dilated by comparison"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [VIEW] Pulmonary vein entry view
- **Depicted Structures**: Pulmonary vein entering the left atrium; the arrow denotes the foramen ovale opening
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"pulmonary vein entering left atrium—arrow indicates opening of foramen ovale"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (1992), *Extended fetal echocardiographic examination for detecting cardiac malformations in low risk pregnancies.* [BMJ]

### [VIEW] Pulmonary venous visualization
 - **Modality**: TVS/TAS with 2D and color Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 10–15 weeks
- **Required Or Attempted Structure**: At least two pulmonary veins were sought for the complete assessment.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"at least 2 pulmonary veins"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Jan Michael Smrcek et al. (2006), *Early Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [VIEW] Upper mediastinal three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Expected Anatomy**: Pulmonary trunk, arterial duct and aorta are the reference vessels; an additional vessel left of the pulmonary trunk and duct suggests PLSVC.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"an abnormal three-vessel view at the upper mediastinum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Isabelle Durand et al. (2022), *Outcomes following prenatal diagnosis of isolated persistent left superior vena cava* [Archives of Cardiovascular Diseases]

### [VIEW] Pulmonary outflow tract view after aortic-arch acquisition
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Tilting after the aortic arch view identifies the main pulmonary artery.
- **Expected Relationship**: Main pulmonary artery is perpendicular to the ascending aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"main pulmonary artery was identified by tilting the transducer"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

## 2. CLINICAL WORKFLOWS & SCREENING PROTOCOLS

### [WORKFLOW] Extended view acquisition from four-chamber plane
- **General Step**: Approximately 90-degree transducer axis rotation after obtaining the four-chamber view brought major veins and arteries into view
- **Lvot Step**: Slight cranial angulation from four-chamber view and slight clockwise rotation when fetal spine was posterior
- **Mpa Step**: Further cranial angulation and counter-clockwise transducer rotation to obtain the pulmonary artery bifurcation
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"simple rotation of the transducer along its axis by about 90° brought the major great veins and major great arteries into view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (1992), *Extended fetal echocardiographic examination for detecting cardiac malformations in low risk pregnancies.* [BMJ]

### [WORKFLOW] Routine fetal cardiac view acquisition in study
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional prenatal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: At at least 17 weeks, the center routinely obtained four-chamber, short-axis, and both outflow-tract views.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber, short axis views and views of the outflow tracts of both great vessels"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Thomas D. Shipp et al. (1995), *Levorotation of the Fetal Cardiac Axis: A Clue for the Presence of Congenital Heart Disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Complete fetal echocardiographic examination sequence
- **Acquisition**: Assess situs and heart position, four-chamber, outflow tracts, three-vessel plane, aortic/ductal arches, systemic and pulmonary venous return
- **Modality**: Use 2D with color/pulsed Doppler
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"observation of the situs, the position of the heart, the four-chamber-view, the outflow tracts, the three-vessel view, the aortic and ductal arches and both systemic and pulmonary venous returns."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: A. Galindo et al. (2007), *Clinical significance of persistent left superior vena cava diagnosed in fetal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Determine ventriculoarterial connection
- **Illustrated Step**: Determine ventriculoarterial connection
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Longitudinal views of fetus show anterior ventricle (morphologically right)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [WORKFLOW] Acquire ductus plane
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Step**: Change angle from tricuspid–pulmonary plane to follow pulmonary trunk posteriorly to ductus and descending aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the pulmonary trunk can be shown sweeping posteriorly and connecting via the ductus arteriosus with the descending aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [WORKFLOW] Echocardiographic dimension and function assessment
 - **Modality**: fetal and neonatal echocardiography
- **Timing**: Atrioventricular valve and ventricular dimensions at end diastole; semilunar valves in systole.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Atrioventricular valves and ventricular dimensions were measured at end-diastole and semilunar valves were measured during systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: L. R. Freud et al. (2015), *Low rate of prenatal diagnosis among neonates with critical aortic stenosis: insight into the natural history in utero* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Routine anomaly scan remains necessary despite NT assessment
- **Limitation And Action**: NT screening does not replace routine fetal-heart assessment at 18–23 weeks
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"it will not replace the need for an adequate assessment of the fetal heart as part of the routine anomaly scan at 18–23 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Ghi et al. (2001), *Incidence of major structural cardiac defects associated with increased nuchal translucency but normal karyotype* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Extended fetal echocardiography acquisition sequence
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Sequence**: Four-chamber view, then about 90-degree probe rotation to the left ventricle outlet, right ventricle short axis with main pulmonary artery, and aortic arch and ductus
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"simple rotation of the probe (≈90°) along its axis brought the major great vessels into view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]

### [WORKFLOW] Interpret TT-ratio study findings
- **Sample Size Limitation**: Small numbers prevented detailed subgroup comparisons.
- **Immune Function Limitation**: No fetal immune-status information was available.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"lack of information regarding the immune status of the fetuses examined"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2012), *Thymic–thoracic ratio in fetuses with trisomy 21, 18 or 13* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Optimize grayscale parameters
- **Recommended Action**: Use high frame rate, contrast, resolution, low persistence, one focus, and a narrow field for grayscale cardiac imaging.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"high frame rate, with increased contrast and high resolution"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Rotate clockwise 90 degrees
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Step**: Rotate the probe 90 degrees clockwise from operator perspective to obtain a transverse fetal thorax image
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The transducer is then rotated clockwise (from the perspective of the echocardiographer) 90 degrees, to visualize optimally a transverse image of the fetal thorax."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [WORKFLOW] Assess for associated malformations after VSD detection
- **Step**: Carefully exclude complex cardiac and extracardiac malformations
- **Step**: Perform complete sequential fetal heart analysis
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Whenever fetal echocardiography reveals a VSD, a complete sequential analysis of the fetal heart is mandatory"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Follow-up of suspected heart defect
- **Trigger And Action**: Physician detailed anatomical survey when a heart defect was diagnosed or suspected; pediatric cardiologist present in most cases.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"When a heart defect was diagnosed or suspected the physicians at the center performed a detailed anatomical survey"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Cine-loop phase selection
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Acquisition**: Freeze the desired view and use the cine loop trackball to select end diastole or systole for the measurement.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the cine loop capability into modern sonographic technology allows measurements from 2-dimensional images during a desired period of the cardiac cycle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Jan Michael Smrcek et al. (2006), *Early Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [WORKFLOW] Select early-gestation four-chamber images
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound, optionally with color Doppler
- **Quality Criterion**: Retain images showing one complete rib on each lateral chest wall and clearly visualized cardiac chambers.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"one complete rib on each side of the fetal lateral chest wall and clear visualization of the cardiac chambers"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Elena S. Sinkovskaya et al. (2015), *Fetal Cardiac Axis and Congenital Heart Defects in Early Gestation* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Evaluate suspected fetal pulmonary stenosis
- **Acquisition Step**: Assess pulmonary valve doming and MPA on sagittal RVOT view, flow turbulence/gradient, RV size/function, ductal direction, tricuspid insufficiency and venous Dopplers.
- **Interpretive Limit**: IVC/ductus venosus atrial-systolic reversal may reflect atrial function rather than solely increased venous pressure.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Smaller RV to LV length, tricuspid and pulmonary valve diameters and tricuspid to mitral valve diameter ratio have also been identified as predictors of a non-biventricular outcome"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [WORKFLOW] Prenatal diagnosis registry definition
- **Measurement Definition**: Age at diagnosis was the first suspicion of any congenital anomaly; prenatal diagnosis could concern CHD or associated non-CHD anomaly.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"defined as first suspicion of any congenital anomaly, whether CHD or associated non-CHD anomaly"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Helen Dolk et al. (2011), *Congenital Heart Defects in Europe* [Circulation]

### [WORKFLOW] Colour-flow assessment of foramen ovale
- **Assessment**: Examine the shunt direction with colour Doppler when available.
- **Interpretation**: A predominant left-to-right pattern may support coarctation when combined with other features.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"12 fetuses with a proved coarctation seven had predominantly a left to right shunt ... five had bidirectional shunting"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [WORKFLOW] Initial increased-NT fetal cardiac assessment
- **Timing**: Initial scan at 10–23 weeks according to NT level
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"An initial fetal cardiac scan was performed at between 10 and 23 weeks of gestation, depending on the level of increased NT"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Ghi et al. (2001), *Incidence of major structural cardiac defects associated with increased nuchal translucency but normal karyotype* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Outflow-tract screening goals
- **Goal Ventricular Origin**: Identify each great artery origin from the appropriate ventricle.
- **Goal Branching**: Identify pulmonary artery bifurcation or aortic-arch branches.
- **Goal Orientation**: Assess perpendicular great-artery exits.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"determine that the pulmonary artery and aorta are perpendicular"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [WORKFLOW] Use transvaginal scan when early transabdominal study is uninformative
 - **Gestational Age**: <14 weeks
- **Corrective Action**: If transabdominal scanning is uninformative or suggests abnormality before 14 weeks, offer complementary transvaginal examination.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"if the transabdominal scan is not informative or in the presence of an abnormality at <14 weeks’ gestation, we routinely offer a transvaginal examination"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [WORKFLOW] Avoid misclassifying myocardial rim as small pericardial effusion
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Interpretation Step**: Evaluate septal continuity and a separate more peripheral rim; acknowledge uncertainty with minute fluid.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"pericardial space does not extend into the septum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Douglas L. Brown et al. (1989), *The peripheral hypoechoic rim of the fetal heart* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [WORKFLOW] Study follow-up after left-axis finding
- **Study Action**: After left-axis deviation, detailed anatomic examination including fetal echocardiography was performed; genetic testing offered individually
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"When left axis deviation was found, a detailed anatomic examination, including echocardiography, was performed and genetic testing was offered on an individualized basis"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R SMITH et al. (1995), *Ultrasonographic left cardiac axis deviation: A marker for fetal anomalies* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Screen four-chamber view and attempt both ventricular outflow tracts
- **Sequence**: Examine the four-chamber view and, when technically feasible, both ventricular outflow tracts.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"if technically feasible ... evaluate both cardiac ventricular outflow tracts"*

### [WORKFLOW] Sweep further cephalad for isolated arch
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Step**: Continue cephalad until only the aortic arch remains in the transverse plane
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"When the transducer is moved further cephalad, only the aortic arch is seen"*

### [WORKFLOW] Color Doppler confirmation after suspicion
- **Step**: Use color Doppler from different planes to confirm a suspected anomaly; do not use one apparently entering pulmonary vein on a four-chamber color image as exclusion.
- **Common Error**: Color Doppler in a single four-chamber plane generated false negative screening impressions in reviewed cases.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"l’examen en Doppler couleur dans des incidences différentes permet de confirmer le diagnostic"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [WORKFLOW] Acquire first-trimester NT measurement
- **Sequence**: Measure maximal NT at 10-14 weeks with CRL 38-84 mm; use transvaginal route when transabdominal nuchal view is inadequate
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Nuchal translucency thickness was measured in viable pregnancies with crown-rump length ... 38-84 mm ... Transvaginal scans were performed in cases where inadequate nuchal views were obtained transabdominally"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Mavrides et al. (2001), *Limitations of using first‐trimester nuchal translucency measurement in routine screening for major congenital heart defects* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Evaluate fetal LSVC for associations
- **Corrective Action**: Perform detailed ultrasound including fetal echocardiography before considering LSVC isolated.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The presence of a LSVC in a fetus should not be considered as a variant before detailed ultrasound evaluation is achieved, including a fetal echocardiogram"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2016), *Intrathymic and other anomalous courses of the left brachiocephalic vein in the fetus* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Estimate ventricular pressure from AV regurgitation jet
 - **Modality**: continuous-wave Doppler
- **Measurement Method**: Apply 4 × velocity squared to AV valve regurgitation jet velocity, with atrial pressure added to estimate ventricular systolic pressure.
- **Interpretive Limit**: This review supplies case estimates and a qualitative differential, not a universally validated cutoff.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"supra-systemic RV pressure (50 mm Hg plus the right atrial pressure)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [WORKFLOW] Authors' screening recommendation
- **Author Recommendation**: Authors propose routine heart-axis assessment with four-chamber screening and further echocardiography plus detailed anatomy if abnormal
- **Author Recommendation**: Authors recommend offering genetic testing when additional abnormal findings are present
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"heart axis estimation should be included with the four-chamber view during the screening evaluation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R SMITH et al. (1995), *Ultrasonographic left cardiac axis deviation: A marker for fetal anomalies* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Study cardiac screening sequence
- **Sequence**: Four-chamber view, then aortic and pulmonic outflow-tract views
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Anatomy of the cardiovascular system was identified by achieving the four-chamber view followed by identification of the aortic and pulmonic outflow tracts."*

### [WORKFLOW] Study cardiac-axis measurement
- **Measurement Step**: Identify fetal left/right by lie and presentation; divide chest from spine to anterior wall; measure suspected angle over 75 degrees on still photograph
- **Measurement Step**: When septum-to-midline angle appeared above 75 degrees, it was measured on a still photograph
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The left and right sides of the fetus were identified by evaluating lie and presentation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R SMITH et al. (1995), *Ultrasonographic left cardiac axis deviation: A marker for fetal anomalies* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Acquire long-axis ductal arch

- **Step**: Align main pulmonary artery and descending aorta in three-vessel plane, rotate approximately 90 degrees, and check that the ductal arch has no head/neck branches

### [WORKFLOW] Historical gestational-age scheduling preference
- **Author Recommendation**: Authors considered examination at 18–21 weeks preferable to 16–18 weeks for cardiac assessment, while their routine program used about 18 weeks
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"18–21 weeks is preferable to one in the 16–18-week period"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1994), *Incorporating the four‐chamber view of the fetal heart into the second‐trimester routine fetal examination* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Acquire LV short-axis plane

- **Step**: Use sagittal cut left of sternum with slight obliquity toward left shoulder.

### [WORKFLOW] Escalate an asymmetric fetal cardiac screen
- **Action**: Perform a more thorough fetal heart examination when asymmetry is seen

### [WORKFLOW] Serial fetal echocardiographic follow-up
- **Assessment Sequence**: Reassess valve obstruction, ventricular function, AV valve function and cardiac growth through gestation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Fetal OTO, most commonly AS and PS, is associated with progressive obstruction in most affected fetuses."*

### [WORKFLOW] Sweep from three-vessel view to 3VT

### [WORKFLOW] Correction for anterior fetal spine
 - **Gestational Age**: 20–24 weeks
- **Error Or Constraint**: Anterior fetal spine relative to cardiac structures impeded the examination

### [WORKFLOW] Further cardiac evaluation after axis levorotation
 - **Modality**: prenatal ultrasound
- **Author Recommendation**: Authors advise careful fetal echocardiographic evaluation after an abnormally leftward axis.
- **Interpretation Limit**: Axis is an indirect clue and a larger prospective study was requested by the authors.

 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed

### [WORKFLOW] Factors that can limit outflow-tract visualization
- **Technical Limitation**: Fetal position can limit visualization.
- **Technical Limitation**: Maternal wall thickness can limit visualization.
- **Technical Limitation**: Gestational age can limit visualization.
- **Technical Limitation**: Acoustic shadowing can limit visualization.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"fetal position, maternal wall thickness, gestational age, and acoustic shadowing"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Ivana M. Vettraino et al. (2005), *Sonographic Evaluation of the Ventricular Cardiac Outflow Tracts* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [WORKFLOW] Transabdominal fetal situs right-hand orientation rule
- **Precondition**: Apply the rule when the displayed ultrasound beam runs from top to bottom.
- **Hand Mapping**: Imagine the examiner’s right hand as the fetus: dorsal forearm as fetal back, palmar forearm as fetal abdomen, and fist as fetal head.
- **Orientation Result**: The examiner’s right thumb indicates fetal left across vertex, breech, oblique, and back-up or back-down presentations.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The thumb will always point to the fetal left side. This is true for all fetal positions"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Bronshtein et al. (2002), *Sonographic definition of the fetal situs* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

- **Quality Check**: Assess strict and slightly anterior planes because inferior and superior pulmonary veins are seen at different levels.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"soit sur une coupe stricte des 4 cavités ... soit sur une coupe un peu plus antérieure"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [WORKFLOW] Acquire fetal three-vessel plane
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Acquisition Step**: Move the transducer cephalad from the four-chamber plane to obtain the upper-mediastinal three-vessel view.
- **Inspection Step**: Assess vessel size, straight-line alignment, left-right arrangement, number and descending-aorta location.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the three vessels are not aligned in a straight line, but their overall left-right order is preserved"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [WORKFLOW] Group-II perpendicular-septum aortic acquisition
- **Condition**: Interventricular septum perpendicular to beam.
- **Action**: Rotate from four-chamber view until aorta from left ventricle, arch and branches are seen.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aortic outflow tract could be observed leaving the left ventricle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [WORKFLOW] Authors' 1992 screening recommendation
- **Recommendation**: At or after 18 weeks, assess both four-chamber and ventricular outflow tract views regardless of risk status
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"all obstetric scans performed at or after 18 weeks' gestation should include evaluation of the ventricular outflow tracts and a four-chamber view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [WORKFLOW] Determine atrial situs
- **Illustrated Step**: Determine atrial situs
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Transverse section through fetus’s upper abdomen demonstrates right-sided abdominal aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [WORKFLOW] Repeat scan after inadequate four-chamber view
- **Trigger**: Offer a repeat at approximately 20 weeks when a proper four-chamber view is not obtained at the routine scan.
- **Acquisition**: Assess four-chamber view, great arteries and venous return.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"20-week scan included assessment of the four-chamber view, the great arteries and the venous return"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

## 3. CONGENITAL HEART DISEASES & PATHOLOGIES

### [DISEASE] Right aortic arch
- **Screening Relevance**: The 3VTV may enable detection of right aortic arch.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"3VTV ... detection of ... right aortic arch"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Partial fetal atrioventricular block
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Some sinus beats conduct, often with 2:1 or 3:2 AV relation and a consistent conducted AV interval; irregular bradycardia may be an early manifestation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"can potentially represent second-degree AV block and be the first manifestation of antibody-mediated block"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Tetralogy of Fallot with subvalvar RV obstruction
- **Mechanism**: Anterior conal septal malalignment produces subvalvar RV outflow obstruction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Subvalvar RVOTO occurs usually as a consequence of anterior malalignment of conal septum as is encountered in tetralogy of Fallot."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [DISEASE] Cervical aortic arch
- **Classification**: Listed as an arch anomaly; Table 1 does not state its ring status
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Cervical AA"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Great-artery lesions
- **Association**: Any asymmetry often involved great-artery lesions; examples included tetralogy of Fallot, coarctation, and transposition
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"tetralogy of Fallot, aortic coarctation, or transposition of the great arteries"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Kirk et al. (1999), *Fetal cardiac asymmetry: a marker for congenital heart disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] D-transposition of the great arteries
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Illustrative Multiview Features**: In the illustrated D-TGA, the 3VTV shows one oblique vessel despite a relatively normal 4CV.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"color Doppler imaging shows only 1 vessel in an oblique fashion instead of 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Interrupted aortic arch
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Tiny ascending aorta in the Figure 2 case; oblique view shows arch interruption.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A small ascending aorta and a large main pulmonary artery were seen in seven fetuses"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Right aortic arch
- **Diagnostic Feature**: U-shaped ductal-aortic configuration, trachea between vessels and arch right of trachea
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Right and double aortic arches were diagnosed when the great vessels appeared U-shaped"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Abnormal fetal situs or situs inversus
- **Diagnostic Context**: Determining fetal right and left axes is relevant to evaluating abnormal situs and related anomalies.
- **Diagnostic Feature**: An abnormal abdominal-to-thoracic organ relationship is a useful pointer.
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Stomach contralateral to the cardiac apex is described as a primary indicator.
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Gallbladder left of the umbilical vein is described as a primary indicator.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"An abnormal relationship between abdominal and thoracic organs is a useful pointer for diagnosis of an abnormal situs or situs inversus."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Bronshtein et al. (2002), *Sonographic definition of the fetal situs* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Aortic valve stenosis
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Poststenotic dilatation of ascending aorta in the illustrated case.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ascending aorta was dilated in a fetus with aortic valve stenosis, owing to post-stenotic dilatation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Ventricular septal defect
- **Detection Limitation**: Small lesions may be below gray-scale ultrasound resolution; some close during pregnancy or soon after birth
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (septal defect).
- **Limitation**: Early detection depends on resolution of septal structures.
- **Early Detection Limit**: Early VSD may be missed on multiple-plane septal imaging.
- **Case Association**: A ventricular septal defect occurred among the additional cardiac findings in this series.
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Interventricular shunting on color Doppler, potentially invisible on gray scale
- **Differential Limit**: Confirm in two planes to avoid apical four-chamber artifact
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a true VSD is confirmed only when it is visible in at least two different planes."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]; M M Abdullah et al. (2000), *Fetal cardiac dextroposition in the absence of an intrathoracic mass: sign of significant right lung hypoplasia.* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Premature or sealed foramen ovale
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasonography
- **Possible Imaging Sign**: In one postmortem-confirmed case, retrospective prenatal video showed ballooning of the foramen-ovale flap into the left atrium rather than normal flapping motion
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"instead of having a normal flapping motion, the foramen ovale showed ballooning into the left atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]

### [DISEASE] Congenital heart disease (study cohort)
- **Chromosomal Association**: 17 of 46 prenatally detected cases had concomitant chromosomal abnormality.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In 17 (37%) a concomitant chromosomal abnormality was found ... In 13 of these 17 cases ... extracardiac abnormalities ... other four ... no risk factors"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Ingrid Stümpflen et al. (1996), *Effect of detailed fetal echocardiography as part of routine prenatal ultrasonographic screening on detection of congenital heart disease* [The Lancet]

### [DISEASE] Primum atrial septal defect
 - **Gestational Age**: first trimester
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (septal defect).
- **Limitation**: Early detection depends on resolution of septal structures.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Primum atrial septal defects"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [DISEASE] Coarctation of the fetal aorta
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography
- **Prenatal Features**: Relative left-heart hypoplasia, aortic/pulmonary disparity and small transverse arch may suggest coarctation.
- **Diagnostic Limit**: No measured feature or combination clearly distinguished proven from false-positive cases, especially in late gestation.
- **Early Limit**: Milder lesions may appear normal on early fetal echocardiography.
- **Functional Association**: Left-to-right foramen-ovale shunting may add diagnostic support with other features.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"none, either alone or in combination, clearly distinguished between real and false positive cases"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [DISEASE] Blocked fetal atrial trigeminy
- **Diagnostic Feature**: A 3:2 AV ratio with premature blocked ectopy yields irregular A–A intervals.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"blocked atrial trigeminy ... three atrial contractions, two consecutive sinus beats are conducted"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Tetralogy of Fallot
- **Screening Relevance**: Outflow-tract and great-vessel assessment may reveal tetralogy of Fallot.
- **Illustrative Multiview Features**: Illustrated ToF with right aortic arch shows axis deviation, a broad single 3VTV vessel, and unequal RVOT signals.
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually normal
- **Detection Limitation**: Pulmonary-artery changes may progress and be subtle on early examinations
- **Screening Limitation**: May not produce an abnormal four-chamber view; outflow views warrant assessment.
- **View Pattern**: 4CV normal; 3VTV and 3VTVC abnormal in Table 2
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Small pulmonary artery and anteriorly displaced aorta; right arch observed in some selected cases.
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Large ascending aorta displaced anteriorly; small main pulmonary artery displaced posteriorly.
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Descending aorta right anterior to spine, abnormal vessel alignment and small main pulmonary artery.
- **Association**: Predominant lesion in great-artery-only asymmetry subgroup
- **Four Chamber View Limitation**: May occur despite a normal-appearing four-chamber view.
- **Figure Appearance**: Anterior aorta despite near-normal 3VV vessel relationship
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"can mimic a normal spatial relationship, yet the aorta is displaced anteriorly"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]; Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Right aortic arch with Kommerell diverticulum
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Dorsal aortic dilatation with aberrant left subclavian artery in one case
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Kommerell’s diverticulum, with aberrant left subclavian artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection
- **Diagnostic Definition**: The study classified PAPVC when three or fewer pulmonary veins failed to drain into the left atrium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"PAPVC was diagnosed when three or fewer pulmonary veins did not drain into"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] tortuous ductus arteriosus
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Ductal loop at left posterior side of main pulmonary artery can mimic an extra vessel.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"forms vascular loop at left posterior aspect of main pulmonary artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [DISEASE] Umbilical vein drainage into coronary sinus
- **Differential**: Can mimic PLSVC when the coronary sinus is dilated.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aberrant drainage of the umbilical vein into a dilated coronary sinus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Isabelle Durand et al. (2022), *Outcomes following prenatal diagnosis of isolated persistent left superior vena cava* [Archives of Cardiovascular Diseases]

### [DISEASE] tricuspid atresia with transposed great arteries and pulmonary atresia
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Illustrative Multiview Features**: Illustrated tricuspid atresia type 2A has one 4CV inflow and abnormal arterial flow across adjacent views.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a singular inflow at the level of the 4-chamber view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Fetal pericardial effusion versus normal myocardial rim
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Differential Feature**: Check septal continuation before labeling a peripheral hypoechoic rim as pericardial fluid.
- **Unresolved Small Fluid Differential**: Small effusion versus minute normal pericardial fluid can be difficult; study provides no quantitative discriminator.
- **Misdiagnosis Caution**: Do not interpret the usual continuous myocardial rim alone as a pericardial effusion.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"pericardial space does not extend into the septum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Douglas L. Brown et al. (1989), *The peripheral hypoechoic rim of the fetal heart* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Hypoplastic left or right heart
- **Association**: Predominant lesion when both ventricular and great-artery diameters were asymmetric
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Both 19 (26) Hypoplastic heart"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Kirk et al. (1999), *Fetal cardiac asymmetry: a marker for congenital heart disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Other univentricular heart defects
- **View Association**: abnormal four-chamber view in author discussion
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"highest prenatal detection rates (>93%) were found in CHD with abnormal four-chamber view (hypoplastic left heart syndrome, other univentricular defects and the complex heart defects with atrial isomerism)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Coarctation or tubular arch hypoplasia
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Small ascending aorta may suggest arch obstruction, but false-positive suspicion occurred.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A small ascending aorta and a large main pulmonary artery were seen in seven fetuses"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Mild/moderate coarctation
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually normal
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mild/moderate coarctation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: GURLEEN K. SHARLAND et al. (1992), *Screening for congenital heart disease prenatally. Results of a 2½‐year study in the South East Thames Region* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Partial vascular ring with right arch and left ductus
- **Association**: Right arch plus left-sided ductus/descending aorta may form a loose partial vascular ring
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"forming a loose partial vascular ring"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Severe coarctation
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually abnormal
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Severe coarctation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: GURLEEN K. SHARLAND et al. (1992), *Screening for congenital heart disease prenatally. Results of a 2½‐year study in the South East Thames Region* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Intracardiac TAPVC to coronary sinus
- **Drainage**: The four pulmonary veins join a broad short collector draining into a dilated coronary sinus.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Les 4 veines pulmonaires se réunissent en un collecteur large et court qui se draine dans le sinus coronaire"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [DISEASE] Mild tricuspid valve abnormality
 - **Gestational Age**: first trimester
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (developmental lesion).
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mild mitral/tricuspid valve abnormalities"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [DISEASE] Vascular ring
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography
- **Definition**: Aortic arch or branch structures form a ring around trachea and esophagus and may compress them.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"vascular rings are congenital abnormalities of the aortic arch and its branches that form a ring around and may compress the trachea and esophagus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] pulmonary valve stenosis
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Main pulmonary artery enlarged by poststenotic dilatation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"main pulmonary artery (P) is enlarged because of poststenotic dilatation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [DISEASE] Minor congenital heart disease (study definition)
- **Classification Limit**: classification of minor defects is arguable; PDA and secundum ASD cannot be detected prenatally due to fetal circulation
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The inclusion of minor defects ... is arguable ... patent ductus arteriosus and ostium secundum atrial septal defects ... cannot be detected prenatally due to the nature of the fetal circulation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Mavrides et al. (2001), *Limitations of using first‐trimester nuchal translucency measurement in routine screening for major congenital heart defects* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Tricuspid valve dysplasia with coarctation
 - **Modality**: transvaginal echocardiography / confirmatory examination as specified
- **Source Described Diagnosis**: In a case with early enlarged right ventricle, autopsy found tricuspid valve dysplasia and coarctation; early atrial septal defect was not confirmed.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"tricuspid valve dysplasia, coarctation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. A. Rustico et al. (2000), *Early screening for fetal cardiac anomalies by transvaginal echocardiography in an unselected population: the role of operator experience* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Fetal valvar aortic stenosis
 - **Modality**: 2D/color/spectral fetal echocardiography
- **Anatomy**: LV obstruction can occur below, at or above the valve; valvar AS has restricted leaflet movement and may have a small annulus and thickened leaflets.
- **Severe Morphology**: Severe AS can have a small aortic valve with progressive aortic root and ascending-aorta hypoplasia.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Left ventricular (LV) OTO can occur at the subvalvar, valvar or supravalvar level."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [DISEASE] aortic arch hypoplasia with ventricular septal defect
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Ascending aorta small, approximately superior vena cava calibre; main pulmonary artery enlarged; minimal alignment distortion.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"small ascending aorta ... Main pulmonary artery is enlarged"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [DISEASE] Pulmonary or aortic stenosis or atresia
- **Screening Limitation**: May not produce an abnormal four-chamber view; outflow views warrant assessment.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"double outlet right ventricle and pulmonary or aortic stenosis or atresia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Persistent left superior vena cava
- **Venous Feature**: In the illustrated case, LSVC is visible with absent LBCV.
- **Evaluation**: Detailed ultrasound and fetal echocardiography are advised before treating fetal LSVC as an isolated variant.
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Extra left-sided vessel in three-vessel view, or abnormal three-vessel arrangement if RSVC absent
- **Prenatal Diagnostic Feature**: Fourth vessel left of pulmonary trunk and ductal arch in three-vessel view.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"an abnormal three-vessel view at the upper mediastinum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Isabelle Durand et al. (2022), *Outcomes following prenatal diagnosis of isolated persistent left superior vena cava* [Archives of Cardiovascular Diseases]; K. Karl et al. (2016), *Intrathymic and other anomalous courses of the left brachiocephalic vein in the fetus* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Common arterial trunk / truncus arteriosus
- **Screening Relevance**: Common arterial trunk typically produces an abnormal three-vessel view.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"common arterial trunk ... typically be abnormal in the 3VV"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Diverticulum of Kommerell
- **Postnatal Anatomy**: Dilated proximal aberrant branch can persist as a diverticulum after ductal closure
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"in a 9-month-old child"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Corrected transposition of great arteries
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Aorta most leftward and anterior; illustrated case also has pulmonary atresia.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four fetuses with complete transposition ... one each ... corrected transposition ... double-outlet right ventricle ... pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Scimitar syndrome
- **Diagnostic Components**: The report describes anomalous right pulmonary venous connection, anomalous right-lung arterial supply, and cardiac dextroposition as components.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"this diagnosis includes anomalous right pulmonary venous connection (partial or complete), typically to the inferior vena cava, portal vein, hepatic vein or right atrium; anomalous arterial supply to the right lower lung, usually from the abdominal aorta; and cardiac dextroposition."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M M Abdullah et al. (2000), *Fetal cardiac dextroposition in the absence of an intrathoracic mass: sign of significant right lung hypoplasia.* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Pulmonary venous return abnormality
 - **Gestational Age**: first trimester
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (venous connection).
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Abnormalities of pulmonary venous return"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [DISEASE] Mitral atresia
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually abnormal
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mitral atresia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: GURLEEN K. SHARLAND et al. (1992), *Screening for congenital heart disease prenatally. Results of a 2½‐year study in the South East Thames Region* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Outlet muscular ventricular septal defect
- **Anatomic Feature**: Defect of muscular outlet septum
- **View Requirement**: Outflow tracts and LV long-axis must be inspected for isolated subarterial outlet defects
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"defects of the inlet and outlet septum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Coarctation of the aorta
- **Screening Relevance**: Ventricular disproportion may prompt consideration of coarctation of the aorta.
- **Screening Relevance**: The 3VTV is particularly useful for evaluating arch abnormalities including coarctation.
- **Sklansky2009 Expected View Pattern**: Both 4CV and OFTVs possibly abnormal
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (developmental lesion).
- **View Pattern**: 4CV normal; 3VTV and 3VTVC abnormal in Table 2 for detected cases
- **Supporting Findings**: Narrow transverse aortic arch; source describes reverse flow and turbulent high-velocity flow in individual detected cases
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"coarctation of the aorta ... important causes of this disparity"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]; Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [DISEASE] Mitral stenosis
 - **Modality**: expected midgestation fetal ultrasound appearance
- **Sklansky2009 Expected 4Cv Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Sklansky2009 Expected Oftv Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mitral stenosis 2 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Complete transposition of great arteries
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Aorta anterior and slightly right of pulmonary artery despite potentially normal four-chamber view.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view is normal ... outflow tracts ... parallel ... ascending aorta ... anteriorly and slightly to the right"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Unbalanced AVC
 - **Modality**: expected midgestation fetal ultrasound appearance

### [DISEASE] Scimitar syndrome
- **Diagnostic Definition**: The authors describe scimitar syndrome as an infradiaphragmatic PAPVC associated with right-lung hypoplasia.
- **Diagnostic Mode**: In the 13 reported scimitar-syndrome cases, color Doppler was used to reach the final diagnosis in all 13.
- **Post La Feature**: In the 13 reviewed scimitar cases, the Table S2 footnote reports no enlarged area or vertical collecting vein behind the left atrium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Diagnosis suspected on CD ... 13/13 (100%)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Left heart hypoplasia
- **Association**: Could emerge or progress as left heart growth slowed

### [DISEASE] DORV
 - **Modality**: expected midgestation fetal ultrasound appearance
- **Sklansky2009 Expected 4Cv Grade**: {'grade': 1, 'meaning': 'normal'}
- **Sklansky2009 Expected Oftv Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"DORV 1 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Left aortic arch with aberrant right subclavian or innominate artery
- **Branch Pattern**: Retroesophageal aberrant right branch follows left-sided head/neck branches
- **Ring Configuration**: Usual left ductus gives incomplete ring; rare right ductus gives complete ring
- **Association**: Review notes association with CHD, especially in Down syndrome cases
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"With left ductus from the aorta                Incomplete
  With right ductus from the aberrant artery     Complete"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Ebstein anomaly
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **View Pattern**: 4CV abnormal; 3VTV and 3VTVC normal in Table 2
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Main pulmonary artery smaller than ascending aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"AVSD / EBSTEIN / HLHS / HRHS: 4CV A, 3-VTV N, 3-VTVC N; TGA / FALLOT / CO.A: 4CV N, 3-VTV A, 3-VTVC A"*

(2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]; S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [DISEASE] Double inlet ventricle
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually abnormal

### [DISEASE] Large ventricular septal defect

- **Early Detection Possibility**: May be detected in the first trimester but may also be overlooked.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Large ventricular septal defects (1)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [DISEASE] congenitally corrected transposition of great arteries
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Aorta left and anterior to main pulmonary artery; aortic and pulmonary positions reversed from normal.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"positions of ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery are reversed"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [DISEASE] TGA
 - **Modality**: expected midgestation fetal ultrasound appearance
- **Sklansky2009 Expected 4Cv Grade**: {'grade': 1, 'meaning': 'normal'}
- **Sklansky2009 Expected Oftv Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"TGA 1 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Double aortic arch
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Two equal-caliber arch limbs seen with color Doppler, forming a true vascular ring
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"double aortic arch with both limbs of equal caliber, demonstrated by color flow"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Pulmonary stenosis
- **Screening Relevance**: Pulmonary stenosis may be detected through semilunar-valve assessment and can progress during pregnancy.
- **Temporal Appearance**: Mild early stenosis may progress to critical stenosis and right-ventricular hypoplasia; serious stenosis may appear after an initially normal early scan
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"mild PS diagnosed early in the second trimester may progress to critical PS and hypoplasia of the right ventricle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Simcha Yagel et al. (1997), *Congenital Heart Defects* [Circulation]; J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Visceral situs inversus
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Liver and stomach occupy opposite screen positions from situs solitus for the same fetal orientation
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"With situs inversus of the viscera, the liver will be to the right of the video screen and the stomach to the left."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [DISEASE] Pulmonic stenosis
 - **Modality**: second-trimester grayscale/color Doppler; fetal echo confirmation
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Pulmonary outflow aliasing or bidirectional flow on color Doppler was the screening feature in illustrated cases.
- **Limitation**: Grayscale MPA dilation or atrial enlargement may be subtle or absent in these cases.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aliasing and possible post-stenotic dilation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Allan S. Nadel et al. (2010), *Addition of Color Doppler to the Routine Obstetric Sonographic Survey Aids in the Detection of Pulmonic Stenosis* [Fetal Diagnosis and Therapy]

### [DISEASE] Evolving hypoplastic left heart syndrome
- **Screening Relevance**: Evolving hypoplastic left heart syndrome may cause midgestation ventricular size disparity.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"evolving hypoplastic left heart syndrome ... causes of this disparity"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Tetralogy of Fallot with normal-sized pulmonary arteries
 - **Gestational Age**: first trimester
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (outflow lesion).
- **Limitation**: Early detection depends on degree of outflow obstruction and size of main pulmonary artery.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"degree of outflow tract obstruction and size of main pulmonary artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [DISEASE] Vascular ring around trachea and esophagus
- **Clinical Association**: Aortic vascular rings may compress trachea or esophagus, though clinical expression varies
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"complete or incomplete vascular ring around the trachea and esophagus causing compression of the latter structures"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Low atrial rhythm in left atrial isomerism
- **Differential**: A low atrial rhythm in left atrial isomerism is an alternative to sinus bradycardia with 1:1 conduction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"often indicates sinus bradycardia ... may also represent a low atrial rhythm"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Hypoplastic left heart syndrome in Kipps 2011 cohort
 - **Modality**: fetal and postnatal echocardiography
- **Study Definition**: Normal cardiac topology and concordant atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial relations with intact ventricular septum and left-ventricular hypoplasia precluding biventricular repair.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"normal cardiac topology with concordant atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial relations, an intact ventricular septum, and hypoplasia of the left ventricle sufficient to preclude biventricular repair"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Alaina K. Kipps et al. (2011), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome in Current Era* [The American Journal of Cardiology]

### [DISEASE] Severe AS
 - **Modality**: expected midgestation fetal ultrasound appearance
- **Sklansky2009 Expected 4Cv Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Sklansky2009 Expected Oftv Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Severe AS 2 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Valvular anomalies, biventricular heart
- **Screening Limitation**: subtle early appearance; color Doppler often needed
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Valve abnormalities can be very subtle in the first half of pregnancy and usually need the use of colour Doppler. Doppler was not compulsory"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Fetal congenital heart block
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography
- **Diagnostic Context**: Fetal bradycardia may reflect atrioventricular block; complete block may coexist with heterotaxy, atrioventricular septal defect, or corrected transposition, or with maternal anti-Ro/anti-La autoantibodies.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"These are usually either abnormalities of situs (the heterotaxy syndromes, including left and right atrial isomerism) or other lesions, such as atrioventricular septal defects and corrected transposition"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. Small et al. (2004), *Indications for Fetal Echocardiography* [Pediatric Cardiology]

### [DISEASE] TGA with associated ventricular septal defect
- **Association**: TGA may be accompanied by VSD; associated four-chamber abnormalities can act as a screening clue.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"TGA may be isolated or occur in association with another cardiac defect, such as a septal defect"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Blyth et al. (2008), *The hidden mortality of transposition of the great arteries and survival advantage provided by prenatal diagnosis* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian or innominate artery
- **Anatomical Course**: Aberrant left branch arises distally and passes behind trachea and esophagus
- **Diagnostic Feature**: With left ductus, a U-shaped axial ring forms around the trachea
- **Flow**: Proximal aberrant branch carries fetal ductal flow toward descending aorta
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Right aortic arch (AA) with aberrant left subclavian artery and left ductus arteriosus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Double aortic arch
 - **Modality**: 2D and color fetal echocardiography
- **Diagnostic Features**: Left and right aortic arches are seen on opposite sides of the trachea, with a ring confirmed by color flow.
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Both arch limbs encircle trachea/esophagus; axial ring may appear 6- or 9-shaped
- **Ring Status**: Table 1 classifies either ductus-side configuration as complete ring
- **Limitation**: An atretic limb is difficult to distinguish from a unilateral arch with aberrant branching
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"appearance of a figure of ‘6’ or ‘9’"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]; Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Pathological fetal atrioventricular block
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Regular A–A intervals with failed atrioventricular conduction indicate pathological AV block.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"related to transplacental transfer ... maternal antibodies ... associated with congenital heart disease"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Tricuspid atresia
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually abnormal

Results of a 2½‐year study in the South East Thames Region* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]; Julene S. Carvalho et al. ### [DISEASE] common arterial trunk
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed

### [DISEASE] Perimembranous ventricular septal defect
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Perimembranous defect with bidirectional interventricular jet on spectral Doppler

### [DISEASE] Double-outlet right ventricle
- **Screening Relevance**: Outflow-tract and great-vessel views support detection of double-outlet right ventricle.

- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually normal
- **Four Chamber Detection Limitation**: This 1995 study reports that double-outlet right ventricle may have normal four-chamber view at 18 weeks.
- **Screening Limitation**: May not produce an abnormal four-chamber view; outflow views warrant assessment.
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Side-by-side great arteries with disturbed linear alignment in illustrated cases.
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery side by side.
- **Four Chamber View Limitation**: May occur despite a normal-appearing four-chamber view.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"right heart dominance ... communication between the ventricles"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]; G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Hypoplastic left heart syndrome
- **Sklansky2009 Expected View Pattern**: Both 4CV and OFTVs abnormal
- **Illustrative Multiview Features**: In the illustrated HLHS case, a broad vertical 3VTV arm corresponds to enlarged pulmonary artery/ductus, with retrograde aortic-arch flow.
- **View Association**: abnormal four-chamber view in author discussion
- **Association Count**: {'pulmonary venous anomaly': 7}
- **Early Detection Possibility**: May be detected in the first trimester.
- **View Pattern**: 4CV abnormal; 3VTV and 3VTVC normal in Table 2
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Tiny ascending aorta displaced posteriorly; markedly dilated main pulmonary artery.
- **Study Case Definition**: Normal topology and concordant AV/VA connections; intact ventricular septum; left ventricle and left-heart complex too hypoplastic for biventricular repair
- **Prenatal Appearance**: Small left side or echogenic left ventricle on four-chamber view
- **Associated Flow**: Left-to-right foramen ovale shunting and often retrograde aortic arch flow described by the authors
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"HLHS with a pulmonary venous anomaly 7"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]; CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]
