 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Illustrative Multiview Features**: Illustrated DILV with transposed arteries has one 4CV inflow and one oblique 3VTV artery.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a singular inflow was found; the 3-vessel and trachea view shows a singular arterial vessel in an oblique fashion"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Aortic arch anomaly
- **Definition**: Congenital abnormality of arch position, branching pattern, or both
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Aortic arch anomalies refer to congenital abnormalities of the position or branching pattern, or both of the aortic arch"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Secondary ventricular outflow tract obstruction
- **Association**: Altered ventricular function or output can contribute to semilunar obstruction, including in recipient twins with twin–twin transfusion syndrome.
- **Differential**: AV-valve regurgitation jet velocity can help distinguish low-pressure secondary from high-pressure primary obstruction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"low ventricular systolic pressures by CW Doppler interrogation of AV valve insufficiency jet can assist in differentiating the primary from the secondary lesion"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [DISEASE] complete transposition of great arteries
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Illustrated Diagnostic Features**: Ascending aorta right and anterior to main pulmonary artery; grossly distorted three-vessel alignment.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"gross distortion of three-vessel alignment"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [DISEASE] Critical aortic stenosis
 - **Modality**: obstetric ultrasound
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually abnormal
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Critical aortic stenosis"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: GURLEEN K. SHARLAND et al. (1992), *Screening for congenital heart disease prenatally. Results of a 2½‐year study in the South East Thames Region* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [DISEASE] Complete fetal atrioventricular block
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Atrial and ventricular contractions are temporally independent, with no AV conduction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"2:1 partial AV block ... atrial contractions are completely independent"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Atrioventricular septal defect
- **Screening Relevance**: Abnormal atrioventricular valve alignment is a clue to atrioventricular septal defect.
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually abnormal
- **Diagnostic Feature**: Abnormal four-chamber view is described as characteristic.
- **Four Chamber Detection Limitation**: This 1995 study reports that atrioventricular septal defect abnormal four-chamber view expected for the missed Phase II twin case.
- **Source Described Diagnosis**: Four atrioventricular defects (three complete, one incomplete) in Table 2 were missed at early transvaginal screening.
- **Early Detection Limitation**: May be overlooked at first-trimester scan (septal defect).
- **Limitation**: Early detection depends on resolution of septal structures.
- **Early Detection Possibility**: Can be detected in the first trimester but may also be overlooked.
- **View Pattern**: 4CV abnormal; 3VTV and 3VTVC normal in Table 2
- **Association**: AVSD predominated with ventricular-only asymmetry and also appeared among no-asymmetry lesions
- **Association**: Common in heterotaxy-associated PLSVC; often unbalanced with right isomerism
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"almost all fetuses with left isomerism showed azygos continuation of an interrupted inferior vena cava (5/6, 83%) and the most common CHD was also AVSD (50%)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]; Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]

### [DISEASE] L-TGA
 - **Modality**: expected midgestation fetal ultrasound appearance
- **Sklansky2009 Expected 4Cv Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Sklansky2009 Expected Oftv Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"L-TGA 3 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Primary fetal bradycardia
- **Definition**: Slow fetal heart rate from the heart's conduction system and/or myocardium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"‘primary bradycardia’: the occurrence of slow fetal heart rate ... related directly to the heart"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Main pulmonary artery may be absent; branch pulmonary arteries form a confluence behind the anterior aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four fetuses with complete transposition ... one each ... corrected transposition ... double-outlet right ventricle ... pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Suspected truncus arteriosus, unconfirmed
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Source Diagnosis Status**: Figure 9 explicitly labels truncus arteriosus as not confirmed.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Truncus arteriosus (not confirmed). (a) Three-vessel view, showing that a single arterial trunk (T) is located in the right anterior aspect of the superior vena cava (V). The pulmonary artery (P) arises from the posterior wall of the trunk. (b) Oblique sagittal view of the fetal thorax, showing that a single "*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Transposition of the great arteries
- **Screening Relevance**: Outflow-tract and great-vessel views support detection of transposition, which may be missed in four-chamber view.
- **Screening Feature**: Parallel great vessels were recommended as a fetal ultrasound screening clue.
- **Study Four Chamber Classification**: Classified as likely normal on the screening four-chamber view for this analysis.
- **Screening View Relevance**: Described as requiring outflow tract views for diagnosis in screening.
- **Usual Four Chamber Appearance**: usually normal
- **Classification**: simple TGA with/without VSD, complex TGA
- **Screening Limitation**: May not produce an abnormal four-chamber view; outflow views warrant assessment.
- **View Pattern**: 4CV normal; 3VTV and 3VTVC abnormal in Table 2
- **Figure Appearance**: Anterior aorta and pulmonary artery not visible in depicted 3VV
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"tetralogy of Fallot and transposition of the great arteries may not be visualized"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Michael D. Quartermain et al. (2015), *Variation in Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease in Infants* [Pediatrics]; Antongiulio Del Bianco et al. (2006), *Four chamber view plus three-vessel and trachea view for a complete evaluation of the fetal heart during the second trimester* [Journal of Perinatal Medicine]

### [DISEASE] Small ventricular septal defect
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: approximately 18 weeks
- **Four Chamber Detection Limitation**: This 1995 study reports that small ventricular septal defect may have normal four-chamber view at 18 weeks.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"will most likely have a normal four-chamber view at 18 weeks of gestation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Persistent left superior vena cava
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Extra vessel left posterior to pulmonary artery; may connect to coronary sinus.
- **Differential**: A left vertical vessel can be persistent left superior vena cava rather than a supracardiac pulmonary venous collector; TAPVC and left SVC may also coexist.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ascending aorta was dilated in a fetus with aortic valve stenosis, owing to post-stenotic dilatation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]; S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [DISEASE] Ebstein anomaly with pulmonary obstruction
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Three Vessel Feature**: Small main pulmonary artery with enlarged aorta in illustrated stenotic Ebstein anomaly.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A small main pulmonary artery and a large ascending aorta were seen in four fetuses"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

## 4. SONOGRAPHIC FINDINGS & DIAGNOSTIC FEATURES

### [FINDING] Right pulmonary vein visualization difficulty
- **Observed Appearance**: Right pulmonary veins were difficult to visualize on imaging and color flow mapping except in one case with suspected connection to the right atrium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The right pulmonary veins were difficult to visualize by imaging and by color flow mapping in all but one case"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M M Abdullah et al. (2000), *Fetal cardiac dextroposition in the absence of an intrathoracic mass: sign of significant right lung hypoplasia.* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Peripheral hypoechoic rim within fetal ventricular myocardium
 - **Modality**: ultrasound
- **Figure 1A Appearance**: Four-chamber image at 29 weeks shows peripheral hypoechoic LV wall rim (arrow).
- **Anatomic Interpretation**: Rim is intramyocardial and can appear nearly anechoic, potentially simulating fluid.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"rim ... is intrinsic to the myocardium and not due simply to refraction artifact"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Douglas L. Brown et al. (1989), *The peripheral hypoechoic rim of the fetal heart* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Physiologic fetal pericardial fluid
 - **Gestational Age**: 19–38 weeks
- **Appearance**: An echo-free rim may be seen along ventricles and the atrioventricular junction.
- **Interpretation**: Presence alone is not considered abnormal in the stated cohort.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The presence of pericardial fluid per se should not be considered as abnormal when it does not exceed 2 mm"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2001), *Normal pericardial fluid in the fetus: color and spectral Doppler analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Only two vessels in three-vessel plane
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Two visible vessels are described in truncus arteriosus; they can also occur with pulmonary atresia and ventricular septal defect if the main pulmonary artery is atretic or absent.
- **Illustrated In Case**: Figure 12: Only two visible vessels: superior vena cava on right and common arterial trunk on left.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"only two vessels: superior vena cava ... and common arterial trunk"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [FINDING] Septum primum at cardiac crux
- **Criterion**: The septum primum should be visible near the cardiac crux.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"septum primum, should be present and forms part of the cardiac crux"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Chamber symmetry assessed
 - **Modality**: second-trimester fetal ultrasound
- **Assessed Structure Or Feature**: symmetry
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"symmetry"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Hautala et al. (2019), *The implementation of a nationwide anomaly screening programme improves prenatal detection of major cardiac defects: an 11‐year national population‐based cohort study* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [FINDING] Right ventricular hypertrophy
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: RV mass can increase as afterload rises in progressive PS.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The RV increases its mass to accommodate the increased afterload"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Stomach contralateral to cardiac apex
- **Indicates**: The fetal stomach on the side opposite the cardiac apex is described as a primary indicator of abnormal situs.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a stomach located contralateral to the apex of the heart"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Bronshtein et al. (2002), *Sonographic definition of the fetal situs* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Severe AS
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Severe AS 2 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Levocardia apex direction with fetus right side up
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Cardiac Apex Screen Direction**: bottom
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Right Side Up Levocardia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [FINDING] Thickened doming pulmonary valve
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: A doming pulmonary valve is a described sign of evolving valvar PS.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a doming pulmonary valve (Fig. 5) and mildly dilated main pulmonary artery"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] RV/LV diameter ratio measurement
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Method**: RV and LV diameters measured from inner myocardial wall to inner septal wall at AV valve level in diastole, then ratio RV/LV
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Ventricles were measured from the inner edge of the myocardial wall to the inner edge of the septal wall"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Kirk et al. (1999), *Fetal cardiac asymmetry: a marker for congenital heart disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Single ventricle
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Single ventricle 3 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Ventriculoarterial connections in TGA
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography
- **Anatomical Criterion**: Aorta connected to right ventricular outflow tract; pulmonary artery connected to left ventricular outflow tract.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aorta and pulmonary artery are connected to the right and left ventricular outflow tracts, respectively"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Blyth et al. (2008), *The hidden mortality of transposition of the great arteries and survival advantage provided by prenatal diagnosis* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [FINDING] Parallel great vessels in fetal screening
 - **Modality**: ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 18-week routine scan in authors' recommendation
- **Appearance**: Parallel great vessels were proposed as a screening clue for transposition of the great arteries.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"detection of parallel great vessels in the routine fetal ultrasound screening at 18 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Damien Bonnet et al. (1999), *Detection of Transposition of the Great Arteries in Fetuses Reduces Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality* [Circulation]

### [FINDING] 3VT: Two symmetrical filling flow patterns
 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler
- **Quality Criterion**: Two symmetrical filling flow patterns
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Two symmetrical filling flow patterns"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Quarello et al. (2017), *Basic heart examination: feasibility study of first-trimester systematic simplified fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Obstructive cardiac lesion may develop or progress after 20 weeks
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Temporal Limitation**: may develop or progress after 20-week scan
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"obstructive lesions can develop or progress as pregnancy advances and may not be recognisable around 20 weeks of gestation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [FINDING] Association: Tetralogy of Fallot with agenesis of corpus callosum, clenched fingers, IUGR
- **Source Observed Association**: Among total-population CHD cases with normal karyotype, Table 9 reports one critical case with tetralogy of fallot and associated agenesis of corpus callosum, clenched fingers, iugr.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Tetralogy of Fallot  agenesis of corpus callosum, clenched fingers, IUGR  1"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Smooth left ventricular apex
- **Criterion**: The morphological left ventricular apex appears smooth and forms the cardiac apex.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"left ventricular apex appears smooth"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Hydrops from progressive outflow disease
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Severe hemodynamic compromise can progress to fetal hydrops.

### [FINDING] Eight-plane anatomical assessment
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Severe PS
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}

- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Pulmonary venous atrial-systolic reversal
 - **Modality**: spectral Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Pulmonary venous atrial-systolic flow reversal can accompany rising LA pressure.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Pulmonary venous Dopplers demonstrate decreasing early diastolic forward flow and often retrograde flow during atrial systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Proximal aberrant branch ductal flow toward descending aorta
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Functional Criterion**: Proximal aberrant left branch conducts fetal ductal flow toward descending aorta in the illustrated configuration
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"blood flow through it is reversed"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Short right ventricular inflow duration
 - **Modality**: spectral Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Shorter RV inflow duration has been reported with progressive RV hypoplasia.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Shorter duration RV inflow ... has been identified as a predictor of progressive hypoplasia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Prenatal pulmonary venous obstruction
- **Measurement Definition**: The study defined prenatal pulmonary venous obstruction as flow velocity above 0.5 m/s and/or loss of the usual pulsatile flow pattern.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"flow velocity of > 0.5 m/s and/or loss of classic pulsatile flow"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Interventricular communication in illustrated DORV
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated DORV 4CV shows communication between ventricles.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"communication between the ventricles"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Cardiac axis angle definition
- **Measurement Definition**: Angle between the thoracic midline and the line along the interventricular septum to its intersection with the anterior chest wall, in the four-chamber plane
- **Method**: On a four-chamber image, draw a spine-to-anterior-chest-wall line bisecting the thorax; measure its angle with the ventricular septum using a protractor.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The cardiac axis is defined as the angle between a line dividing the thorax into two equal halves and where the interventricular septum intersects the anterior chest wall"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Thomas D. Shipp et al. (1995), *Levorotation of the Fetal Cardiac Axis: A Clue for the Presence of Congenital Heart Disease* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]; R SMITH et al. (1995), *Ultrasonographic left cardiac axis deviation: A marker for fetal anomalies* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Superior vena cava dilatation

- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: An enlarged superior vena cava can occur with interrupted inferior vena cava with azygos/hemiazygos continuation or right-heart failure.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Dilatation of the superior vena cava occurs when there is an interruption of the inferior vena cava"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [FINDING] Left-sided V sign
- **Criterion**: The normal aortic and ductal arches form an acute V configuration left of the trachea.

### [FINDING] Normal left V-shaped arch confluence
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Normal Appearance**: Left aortic and ductal arches join at descending aorta in a V or Y configuration
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"both the aortic arch and left ductus arteriosus are visualized forming a ‘V’-shaped confluence"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Discordant abdominal and thoracic organ relationship
- **Indicates**: An unusual relationship between abdominal and thoracic organs is a diagnostic pointer for abnormal situs or situs inversus.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"An abnormal relationship between abdominal and thoracic organs is a useful pointer for diagnosis of an abnormal situs or situs inversus."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Bronshtein et al. (2002), *Sonographic definition of the fetal situs* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] 4CV: Two separate atrioventricular filling flow patterns, from atria to apex of ventricles
 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler
- **Quality Criterion**: Two separate atrioventricular filling flow patterns, from atria to apex of ventricles
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Two separate atrioventricular filling flow patterns, from atria to apex of ventricles"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Quarello et al. (2017), *Basic heart examination: feasibility study of first-trimester systematic simplified fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Independent atrial and ventricular activity
 - **Modality**: M-mode or pulsed-wave Doppler
- **Appearance**: Complete AV block shows no fixed temporal relation between atrial and ventricular systoles.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"2:1 partial AV block ... atrial contractions are completely independent"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Normal AV valve offset
- **Criterion**: The septal tricuspid leaflet inserts more apically than the mitral leaflet.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"tricuspid valve ... closer to the apex ... compared with ... mitral valve"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Rounded left atrium
- **Abnormal Appearance**: A rounded left atrium was noted in slightly more than half of the reviewed cases, so absence does not rule out TAPVC.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"L’aspect arrondi de l’oreillette gauche est noté dans un peu plus de la moitié des cas"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [FINDING] TGA appearance in three-vessel view
 - **Modality**: grayscale ultrasound
- **Study Observation**: Anterior aortic displacement and pulmonary artery not seen in the view
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the aorta is displaced anteriorly, and the pulmonary artery is not visible as it emerges from the heart below this plane"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Sheila M.P. Everwijn et al. (2018), *The effect of the introduction of the three‐vessel view on the detection rate of transposition of the great arteries and tetralogy of Fallot* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [FINDING] Cardiac-axis deviation in illustrated ToF
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated ToF/right-aortic-arch case has a deviated cardiac axis on 4CV.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Deviation of the cardiac axis is shown at the level of the 4-chamber view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Blocked atrial trigeminy timing
- **Appearance**: Two of three atrial contractions conduct; a premature blocked ectopic beat makes A–A intervals irregular.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"blocked atrial trigeminy ... three atrial contractions, two consecutive sinus beats are conducted"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Cephalad branches of fetal aortic arch
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Anatomical Criterion**: Brachiocephalic and common carotid arteries branch cephalad from the aortic arch.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"brachiocephalic and common carotid arteries branching cephalad"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Dextrocardia apex direction with fetus left side up
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Cardiac Apex Screen Direction**: bottom
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Left Side Up Dextrocardia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [FINDING] Reduced left ventricular systolic function
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Worsening AS may lead to LV dilation and reduced systolic function.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the LV became dilated with reduced systolic function"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Regular atrial-to-atrial interval with blocked beats
- **Appearance**: Regular A–A intervals when atrial rate exceeds ventricular rate support pathological AV block.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"atrial contractions is regular ... some or all of these are not transmitted ... pathological heart block"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Face-down transverse laterality
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography | **Gestational Age**: not stated
- **Screen Orientation**: Fetal left is on screen left
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the fetus' left side will be on the left of the video screen."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [FINDING] Ventricles approximately equal
- **Criterion**: In midgestation the ventricles should be approximately equal in size.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Both ventricles should appear similar in size"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Gestational-age-specific fifth-centile FHR examples
 - **Gestational Age**: 25, 30 and 40 weeks
- **Range**: Cited fifth-centile baseline FHR is about 135 bpm at 25 weeks, 125 bpm at 30 weeks, 120 bpm at 40 weeks.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"5th centile is around 135 bpm at 25 weeks, 125 bpm at 30 weeks and 120 bpm at 40 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Resuscitation failure and atrial septal restriction
 - **Modality**: postnatal clinical and echocardiographic assessment
- **Observed Association**: 8 resuscitation failures: 4 preDx and 4 postDx; 6 of 8 had intact or very restrictive atrial septum.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Resuscitation failure occurred in 8 patients, 4 in each group ... 6 were born with an intact or very restrictive atrial septum"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Alaina K. Kipps et al. (2011), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome in Current Era* [The American Journal of Cardiology]

### [FINDING] Left-to-right foramen ovale flow
 - **Modality**: color Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Elevated left atrial pressure can reverse foramen-ovale flow from left to right.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"reversal of flow through the foramen ovale from left to right atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Mitral atresia
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mitral atresia 3 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Maternal adipose thickness measurement method
- **Measurement Definition**: Thickness of maternal adipose tissue overlying uterus in the plane of the imaged heart
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"thickness of the maternal adipose tissue overlying the uterus in the plane of the imaged heart"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1993), *Fetal echocardiography: factors that influence imaging of the fetal heart during the second trimester of pregnancy* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Retrograde aortic arch flow in HLHS
 - **Modality**: color-flow Doppler
- **Flow Direction**: Retrograde aortic arch flow
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"often retrograde aortic arch flow"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Wayne Tworetzky et al. (2001), *Improved Surgical Outcome After Fetal Diagnosis of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome* [Circulation]

### [FINDING] Aortic valve Doppler gradient
 - **Modality**: spectral Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Moderate AS commonly has a measurable LVOT gradient.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In moderate AS, there is typically a measurable Doppler gradient through the LV outflow tract, evolution of LV hypertrophy with preserved systolic function, and, in some, evolution of mitral valve insufficiency."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Abnormal abdominal pulmonary venous collector
- **Abnormal Appearance**: An abnormal vessel on the axial abdominal view can be an infracardiac collector; portal drainage strengthens concern.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Toute image vasculaire abdominale anormale doit être expertisée ... surtout si ce vaisseau se draine dans la veine porte"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [FINDING] Three-vessel abnormal vessel-size pattern
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Appearance**: Relative vessel sizes differ from the expected pulmonary artery > aorta > SVC order.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Groups of abnormal three-vessel views and congenital heart diseases"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Normal tracheal position
- **Normal Appearance**: Trachea lateral and posterior to the ductal-aortic junction, with arch to its left
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"trachea in this view should be located laterally and posteriorly to the vessel junction"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Great arteries similar in size
- **Criterion**: The great arteries should be approximately equal in size; a major discrepancy warrants further evaluation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"great arteries are approximately equal in size"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] First-trimester nuchal translucency measurement
- **Measurement Image**: maximal NT thickness
- **Study Upper Limit Normal**: 2.5 mm (95th centile during study)
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"During the study period, an NT thickness of 2.5 mm was considered to be the upper limit of normal (95th centile)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Mavrides et al. (2001), *Limitations of using first‐trimester nuchal translucency measurement in routine screening for major congenital heart defects* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] U-shaped right-arch/left-ductus loop
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Right arch and left ductus/aberrant branch form a U-shaped axial vascular loop around trachea
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"‘U’-shaped vascular loop is formed around the trachea"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Prominent coronary sinus in fetal four-chamber view
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound
- **Appearance**: Unusually prominent space posterior to left atrium in four-chamber or caudal transverse plane
- **Measurement Method**: Judged subjectively; not routinely quantified
- **Diagnostic Limit**: Indirect sign may have false-negative and false-positive results and can resemble ASD/AVSD
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"an enlarged coronary sinus can be mistaken for an atrial septal defect or even an AVSD in fetal life"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: A. Galindo et al. (2007), *Clinical significance of persistent left superior vena cava diagnosed in fetal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right ventricular moderator band
- **Criterion**: The moderator band near the apex identifies the morphological right ventricle.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"moderator band ... seen near the apex"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right-heart dominance in illustrated DORV
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated DORV case has right-heart dominance on 4CV.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"right heart dominance is shown"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Aortic-valve peak velocity
- **Mid Gestation At Diagnosis N5**: 1.0–1.4
- **Late Gestation At Diagnosis N5**: 2.4–3.7
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"mid-gestation (n = 5) and late gestation (n = 5) and at time of last fetal study (n = 10)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: L. R. Freud et al. (2015), *Low rate of prenatal diagnosis among neonates with critical aortic stenosis: insight into the natural history in utero* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Atrioventricular valves and crux
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional obstetric ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: offset atrioventricular valve attachment at crux
- **Anatomic Relationship**: atrioventricular valves meet septa at crux in offset cross-appearance
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"meet the atrial and ventricular septa at the crux"*

### [FINDING] Subtle ventricular size discrepancy with hypoplastic aorta
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Source Described Appearance**: subtle ventricular size discrepancy with hypoplastic aorta
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Four-chamber view of heart in 20-week fetus with hypoplastic aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Posterior displacement of ascending aorta
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Posterior aortic displacement can suggest severe left-sided obstructive disease such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome or interrupted aortic arch.

- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ascending aorta (A) is tiny and is displaced posteriorly"*

### [FINDING] Tricuspid regurgitation on four-chamber color Doppler
- **Appearance**: Color Doppler showed tricuspid regurgitation when RA enlargement was not evident on grayscale screening.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"routine obstetrical ultrasound at 19 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Allan S. Nadel et al. (2010), *Addition of Color Doppler to the Routine Obstetric Sonographic Survey Aids in the Detection of Pulmonic Stenosis* [Fetal Diagnosis and Therapy]

### [FINDING] 3VT: Two antegrade filling flow patterns
 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler
- **Quality Criterion**: Two antegrade filling flow patterns
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Two antegrade filling flow patterns"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Quarello et al. (2017), *Basic heart examination: feasibility study of first-trimester systematic simplified fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Scimitar vein draining right pulmonary veins to caval system
- **Abnormal Appearance**: A vertical scimitar vein collecting blood from the right pulmonary veins and draining to the caval system was another scimitar-syndrome criterion.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"vertical vein (the scimitar vein) collecting blood from the right pulmonary veins"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] First-trimester fetal heart pulse
 - **Modality**: first-trimester fetal ultrasound
- **Measurement Method**: binary presence/absence, no rate measurement
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Heart pulse +/- (no measurement)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Hautala et al. (2019), *The implementation of a nationwide anomaly screening programme improves prenatal detection of major cardiac defects: an 11‐year national population‐based cohort study* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in TAPVR
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"TAPVR 2 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Dilated proximal aberrant branch after ductal closure
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Postnatal Appearance**: Persistently dilated proximal aberrant branch can form a diverticular pouch after birth
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"in a 9-month-old child"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Rightward cardiac apex
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 20 weeks in this case
- **Appearance**: Cardiac apex points right

### [FINDING] One atrial contraction per ventricular contraction
 - **Modality**: M-mode or pulsed-wave Doppler
- **Appearance**: Sequential atrial and ventricular contractions with short AV delay give a 1:1 AV relation.

- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right-side-up fetal laterality
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography | **Gestational Age**: not stated
- **Screen Orientation**: Back appears on screen left; fetal right is toward the top of the screen

### [FINDING] Candy-cane aortic arch
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Normal Appearance**: Long-axis aortic arch has candy-cane shape and head/neck branches

### [FINDING] Low aortic-root to pulmonary-artery ratio

### [FINDING] Early ventricular or great-artery disproportion
- **Interpretation**: Reported as of uncertain significance; may require shorter-interval follow-up.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"isolated tricuspid valve regurgitation and ventricular or great artery disproportion were also considered to have ‘uncertain significance’"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [FINDING] Early fetal valve abnormality can be subtle
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Appearance**: potentially subtle in first half of pregnancy
- **Methodology**: color Doppler often needed
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Valve abnormalities can be very subtle in the first half of pregnancy and usually need the use of colour Doppler. Doppler was not compulsory"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: CL van Velzen et al. (2015), *Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease—results of a national screening programme* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [FINDING] PA/AO diameter ratio measurement
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound

### [FINDING] Double arch encircling trachea
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Right and left arch limbs surround trachea/esophagus as a complete vascular ring

### [FINDING] Descending aorta crosses back left in circumflex example

- **Appearance**: Trivial-to-mild flow acceleration across a thickened and/or dysplastic aortic valve in five mid-gestation diagnoses.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"trivial to mild flow acceleration across the aortic valve ... thickened and/or dysplastic"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: L. R. Freud et al. (2015), *Low rate of prenatal diagnosis among neonates with critical aortic stenosis: insight into the natural history in utero* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Normal three-vessel caliber order
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: Pulmonary artery is largest, aorta smaller, SVC smallest.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"arranged in a straight line from the left anterior to the right posterior aspect ... decreasing order of their diameters"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Arches on both sides of trachea in coronal plane
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Coronal sonogram may show an arch on each side of trachea, but this has an aberrant-branch differential

- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Abnormal cardiac axis
- **Criterion**: An abnormal cardiac axis raises concern for cardiac malformation, particularly of the outflow tracts.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"abnormal cardiac axis increases the risk of a cardiac malformation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

- **Mean Sd Range Weeks**: {'mean': 25.2, 'range': [13, 39], 'sd': 4.4}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mean gestational age for the 455 encounters was 25.2±4.4 weeks (range 13–39 weeks)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bettina F. Cuneo et al. (2019), *Risk Stratification of Fetal Cardiac Anomalies in an Underserved Population Using Telecardiology* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right-sided filling stripe in illustrated HLHS
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated HLHS four-chamber view shows a right-sided filling stripe.

 - **Modality**: serial 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Method**: Track LV width relative to gestational-age mean across scans.

 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Right ventricular infundibulum ascends anterosuperiorly in LV short-axis plane.

### [FINDING] Complete cardiac visualization at early TV scan

### [FINDING] Mitral valve orifice below gestational range

- **Mean Range**: 23.4 weeks, range 13–39 weeks

### [FINDING] Uniphasic left ventricular inflow

- **Clinical Evidence**: *"blocked atrial bigeminy ... FHR around 70–80 bpm ... 45% of all cases"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Outflow tract views appearance in Mitral atresia
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mitral atresia 3 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Right or midline descending-aortic position
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Abnormal Position**: Right/midline descending aorta is an arch-anomaly clue but has multiple differential diagnoses
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"descending aorta is seen on the right side or in the midline"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right atrial caval connections
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Right atrium is identified by superior and inferior caval venous connections.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The right atrium is recognised by identifying its connection to the superior and inferior vena cavae."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Cardiac situs assessed
 - **Modality**: second-trimester fetal ultrasound
- **Assessed Structure Or Feature**: situs
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"situs"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J Hautala et al. (2019), *The implementation of a nationwide anomaly screening programme improves prenatal detection of major cardiac defects: an 11‐year national population‐based cohort study* [BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Outflow tract views appearance in Truncus arteriosus
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Truncus arteriosus 1 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Four interventricular septal components
- **Anatomy**: Inlet, membranous, trabecular and outlet components have different embryological origins
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The ventricular septum can be divided into four sections: the inlet, membranous, trabecular, and outlet components, which have different embryological origins."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Displaced tricuspid valve in ebstein's anomaly
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Source Described Appearance**: displaced tricuspid valve in Ebstein's anomaly
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Four-chamber view of heart in 25-week fetus with Ebstein's anomaly"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Turbulent pulmonary valve flow
 - **Modality**: color Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Color Doppler can show turbulence at the pulmonary valve.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"turbulence observed at the level of the pulmonary valve"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Apparently normal four-chamber appearance in isolated D-TGA
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated isolated D-TGA case has an apparently normal four-chamber plane.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"4-chamber view (1) typically shows normal-appearing anatomy"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Increased nuchal translucency inclusion criterion
- **Threshold**: Nuchal translucency thickness above the 95th centile for crown–rump length at 10–14 weeks, among singleton pregnancies.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"nuchal translucency thickness above the 95th centile of the normal range for crown–rump length at 10–14 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. A. Hyett et al. (1997), *Increased nuchal translucency at 10—14 weeks of gestation as a marker for major cardiac defects* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Unbalanced AVC
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Unbalanced AVC 3 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Abnormal ductus venosus end-diastolic flow
 - **Modality**: pulsed-wave Doppler | **Gestational Age**: 11–14 weeks
- **Appearance**: Absent or reversed ductus venosus flow at end diastole on pulsed-wave Doppler was an early risk marker in a selected increased-NT cohort.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"abnormal ductus venosus signal (represented by absence or reversal of flow at end-diastole), 7 had major structural heart disease"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [FINDING] Complete TGA altered great-artery arrangement
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Appearance**: Aorta is anterior and slightly right of pulmonary artery; four-chamber view can appear normal.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"four-chamber view is normal ... outflow tracts ... parallel ... ascending aorta ... anteriorly and slightly to the right"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Association: Ventricular septal defect with micrognathia, misplaced ears, columna defect
- **Source Observed Association**: Among total-population CHD cases with normal karyotype, Table 9 reports one noncritical case with ventricular septal defect and associated micrognathia, misplaced ears, columna defect.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Ventricular septal defect  micrognathia, misplaced ears, columna defect  1"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Cardiac area relative to chest
- **Criterion**: Normal fetal heart area is no greater than about one-third of thoracic area.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"no larger than one-third of the area of the chest"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Relative decline in aortic-root diameter on serial studies
 - **Modality**: serial 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Method**: Track aortic-root diameter relative to gestational-age mean across scans.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Sequential measurements of aortic root diameter expressed as a ratio of the normal mean for the gestational age"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] RV pressure from tricuspid regurgitation jet
 - **Modality**: continuous-wave Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Case TR jet suggests RV pressure of 50 mmHg plus RA pressure, supporting primary pulmonary obstruction.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"supra-systemic RV pressure (50 mm Hg plus the right atrial pressure)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Absent LBCV with persistent LSVC
- **Criterion**: LBCV is absent while a persistent LSVC is visible, with right SVC also present in the prospective cases.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a persistent left superior vena cava (LSVC) is visualized and the left brachiocephalic vein is absent."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2016), *Intrathymic and other anomalous courses of the left brachiocephalic vein in the fetus* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Small/reversed ductus in associated tetralogy
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Functional Criterion**: Associated tetralogy may make the ductus small with reverse or bidirectional flow, limiting detection
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ductus tends to be small and the blood flow through it can be reversed or bidirectional"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Associated ventricular septal defect and detection
- **Association**: A VSD was associated with higher prenatal detection in TGA, arch obstruction and pulmonary atresia groups.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"addition of a ventricular septal defect led to higher PDRs for lesions such as TGA, coarctation of the aorta, and pulmonary atresia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Michael D. Quartermain et al. (2015), *Variation in Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease in Infants* [Pediatrics]

### [FINDING] Right deviation of fetal cardiac axis
 - **Modality**: four-chamber fetal ultrasound
- **Study Criterion**: Axis below the control 2.5th percentile was called right deviation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"below the 2.5th percentile (right deviation)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Elena S. Sinkovskaya et al. (2015), *Fetal Cardiac Axis and Congenital Heart Defects in Early Gestation* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Corrected TGA left-anterior aorta
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Appearance**: Ascending aorta is the most leftward and anterior great vessel.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ascending aorta is the most leftward and anterior of the three vessels"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Mid-thorax heart with left-anterior apex
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: approximately 18 weeks
- **Expected Anatomy**: Mid-thorax heart with left-anterior apex
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"located in the middle of the thorax with the apex pointing toward the left anterior chest wall"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] 4CV: Visualization of spine and initial part of one rib to each side
 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler
- **Quality Criterion**: Visualization of spine and initial part of one rib to each side
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Visualization of spine and initial part of one rib to each side"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Quarello et al. (2017), *Basic heart examination: feasibility study of first-trimester systematic simplified fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Nuchal translucency in PLSVC cohort
- **Study Measurement Definition**: First-trimester NT at or above gestational-age reference 95th centile classified as increased
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"those ≥95th centile of the normal range were considered as abnormal."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: A. Galindo et al. (2007), *Clinical significance of persistent left superior vena cava diagnosed in fetal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right ventricle position and texture
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Right ventricle is anterior to left, with often distinguishable thinner wall and coarser trabeculae.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The right ventricle is seen anterior to the left ventricle, and its thinner wall and coarser trabecular pattern are often distinguishable."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Cephalad-sweep ring recognition in cohort
 - **Modality**: fetal 2D/color echocardiography
- **Source Observation**: All eight prenatally recognized rings were first seen on cephalad gray-scale 3VV sweeps.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Eight patients had a prenatal diagnosis by fetal echocardiography."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Supriya Jain et al. (2010), *Prenatal Diagnosis of Vascular Rings* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Intrathoracic mediastinal diameter
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional ultrasound
- **Measurement Definition**: Distance along a line from the anterior edge of the thoracic vertebral body to the internal edge of the sternum.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"between the anterior edge of the thoracic vertebral body posteriorly and the internal edge of the sternum anteriorly"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2012), *Thymic–thoracic ratio in fetuses with trisomy 21, 18 or 13* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Marked left atrial dilation
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Markedly dilated left atrium can compress the right atrium and right ventricle.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the left atrium was very dilated and there was compression of both right atrium (*) and RV"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Increased area behind left atrium
- **Measurement Definition**: For this study, the area behind the left atrium was increased if a venous confluence/vertical vein was seen there or if the post-LA measure exceeded the cited 1.27 cutoff.

### [FINDING] Tetralogy pulmonary artery size

### [FINDING] Cardiac-axis study limitations
- **Limitation**: Retrospective measurements on one observer's readings, a case-control sample not supporting general-population diagnostic value, and possible unblinding from visibly abnormal four-chamber anatomy limit inference.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"measurement of the cardiac axis was performed retrospectively"*

 - **Modality**: color/directional power Doppler

 - **Modality**: color Doppler fetal ultrasound

 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound

- **Diagnostic Feature**: In one prenatal case a right pulmonary vein was demonstrated connecting to the right atrium, confirming suspected scimitar syndrome.

- **Source Observation**: DAA shows left and right arches on either side of the trachea; arch sizes varied in this series.

- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Aortic arch obstruction 2 2"*

 - **Modality**: color-flow Doppler

- **Criterion**: Aortic arch relation to esophagus can be seen.

### [FINDING] General fetal heart rate range 120–160 bpm
 - **Gestational Age**: general, not age-specific

- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Restricted aortic leaflet motion with possible thickening and small annulus.

### [FINDING] Antegrade non-aliased valve flow

### [FINDING] Septal dropout artifact
- **Criterion**: A beam parallel to the septum can produce a false apparent defect near the crux.

### [FINDING] Four-chamber appearance normal despite tetralogy of fallot
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Source Described Appearance**: four-chamber appearance normal despite tetralogy of Fallot

### [FINDING] Small RV and right valve ratios

### [FINDING] Tricuspid regurgitation grading
