### [FINDING] Ascending aorta diameter
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional echocardiography
- **Measurement Method**: above aortic root during ventricular systole
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"ascending aorta diameter above the aortic root, during ventricular systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [FINDING] Aortic arch head-and-neck branches
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Head and neck arteries ascend from the aortic arch as it continues to descending aorta.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the aortic arch can be traced into the descending aorta. The head and neck arteries are seen ascending from the arch and the relation to the oesophagus is seen"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Vertical vein in TAPVC
- **Abnormal Appearance**: A vertical vein was a frequently reported sonographic feature of prenatally diagnosed TAPVC.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"A vertical vein was detected frequently"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right-sided chamber and vessel enlargement
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Right-sided chamber and vessel enlargement should prompt investigation of TAPVC, but balanced chambers do not exclude it.
- **Limitation**: In the author's reviewed cases, right-sided asymmetry was documented in fewer than half and was late.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"notée dans moins de la moitié des cas, toujours tardive"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [FINDING] Nonidentifiable fetal cardiac axis
 - **Modality**: four-chamber fetal ultrasound
- **Study Criterion**: An absent or nonvisualized interventricular septum makes axis measurement impossible and was classified as nonidentifiable.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"absent or nonvisualized interventicular septum, measurement was impossible to perform"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Elena S. Sinkovskaya et al. (2015), *Fetal Cardiac Axis and Congenital Heart Defects in Early Gestation* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Septated cystic hygroma appearance
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound
- **Abnormal Appearance**: A large, often septated cystic mass at the fetal head or neck differs from nuchal translucency.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"This lesion is typically located in the head and neck region"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. Small et al. (2004), *Indications for Fetal Echocardiography* [Pediatric Cardiology]

### [FINDING] Main pulmonary artery diameter above gestational range
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Limitation**: Many coarctation cases had an absolute diameter within gestational reference.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"above the normal range in 10 (22%) of 46 ... and in five (23%) of 22 ... false positive"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Regular ventricular-to-ventricular interval
- **Appearance**: Equal V–V intervals indicate regular ventricular rhythm but do not identify the mechanism alone.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"equal time intervals between ventricular contractions (regular V-V interval)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Progressive left-heart hypoplasia
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Early critical AS can evolve toward a small LV and left heart by later gestation.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"By 32 weeks the left heart was significantly more diminutive and insufficient to sustain the systemic circulation"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Small normal pericardial fluid
- **Criterion**: A small pericardial fluid layer up to 2 mm at end-systole is commonly normal in the second and third trimesters.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"≤ 2 mm in thickness, at end-systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Fetal cardiac long-axis orientation
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Fetal heart lies more horizontally than neonatal heart, with apex displaced cranially in relation to large fetal liver.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the fetal heart lies in a more horizontal plane than the neonatal heart"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Right pulmonary vein connection to left atrium not demonstrated
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Failure to demonstrate right pulmonary venous connection to the left atrium on color or power Doppler was a scimitar-syndrome criterion.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"failure to demonstrate (on color/power Doppler) the connection"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2018), *Prenatal diagnosis of total and partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection: multicenter cohort study and meta‐analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Gestational-age indexing of fetal cardiac biometry
- **Normalization**: Express each measured dimension relative to its expected mean for gestational age.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"measurements were expressed as a proportion of the expected mean for gestational age"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Coarctation may evade four-chamber view
- **Criterion**: Coarctation of the aorta may not be apparent on the four-chamber view alone.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aortic coarctation ... may not be evident in the four-chamber plane alone"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Septoaortic continuity
- **Normal Criterion**: Demonstrated septoaortic continuity contributes to excluding major structural malformations.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"If normality of situs and cardiac connections, atrioventricular junction, right- and left-sided symmetry and septoaortic continuity can confidently be demonstrated"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (2004), *Fetal heart scanning in the first trimester* [Prenatal Diagnosis]

### [FINDING] Retrograde aortic-arch flow in illustrated HLHS
 - **Modality**: fetal transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound; transvaginal rescue where needed
- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated HLHS aortic arch shows retrograde color flow toward the hypoplastic arch.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"retrograde flow on the lower right side"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Separate freely opening AV valves
- **Criterion**: The mitral and tricuspid valves should be distinct and open separately and freely.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Two distinct atrioventricular valves ... open separately and freely"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Dextrocardia apex direction with fetus face down
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Cardiac Apex Screen Direction**: right
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Face Down Dextrocardia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [FINDING] Association: Ventricular septal defect with pes equino varus, unilateral
- **Source Observed Association**: Among total-population CHD cases with normal karyotype, Table 9 reports one noncritical case with ventricular septal defect and associated pes equino varus, unilateral.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Ventricular septal defect  pes equino varus, unilateral  1"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Aortic wedge atrial relationship
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Aorta appears wedged between right and left atria.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the aorta wedged between the right and left atria"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Gestational age increases probability of image acquisition
- **Study Age Range**: 14–23 weeks; mean 17.6 weeks, SD 1.7
- **Direction Of Association**: Higher gestational age increased imaging probability
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The gestational age studied was from 14 to 23 weeks with a mean of 17.6 weeks"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1993), *Fetal echocardiography: factors that influence imaging of the fetal heart during the second trimester of pregnancy* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Two equal-caliber arch limbs on color Doppler
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Two equal-caliber aortic arch limbs visualized by color flow
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"double aortic arch with both limbs of equal caliber, demonstrated by color flow"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Normal aortic arch
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Source Described Appearance**: normal aortic arch
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Longitudinal view of normal aortic arch (AO)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Bryann Bromley et al. (1992), *Fetal echocardiography: Accuracy and limitations in a population at high and low risk for heart defects* [American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Continuous pulmonary venous pulsed Doppler flow
- **Illustrative Appearance**: Continuous flow in hard-to-see pulmonary veins supported an expert diagnosis in one recent case with pleural effusion and chamber asymmetry.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"un flux continu dans les VP difficiles à voir à permis de faire le diagnostic"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [FINDING] Abnormal three-vessel alignment
 - **Modality**: grayscale 2D fetal sonography
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Vessels no longer form a straight line although their overall left-right order is preserved.
- **Illustrated In Case**: Figure 2: Large ascending aorta displaced anteriorly; small main pulmonary artery displaced posteriorly.
- **Illustrated In Case**: Figure 9: Ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery side by side.
- **Illustrated In Case**: Figure 15: Descending aorta right anterior to spine, abnormal vessel alignment and small main pulmonary artery.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the three vessels are not aligned in a straight line, but their overall left-right order is preserved"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S J Yoo et al. (1999), *Abnormal three-vessel view on sonography: a clue to the diagnosis of congenital heart disease in the fetus.* [American Journal of Roentgenology]

### [FINDING] Partial cardiac visualization at early TV scan
 - **Modality**: transvaginal echocardiography
- **Operational Definition**: Partial visualization was defined as the four-chamber view only.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"partial visualization (four-chamber view only)"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M. A. Rustico et al. (2000), *Early screening for fetal cardiac anomalies by transvaginal echocardiography in an unselected population: the role of operator experience* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Isolated ductal-dependent major CHD detection
 - **Modality**: prenatal ultrasound; postnatal echocardiography/autopsy where applicable
- **View Limitation**: Four-chamber view may be normal in ductal-dependent defects; proposal to add three-vessel/color Doppler imaging is untested here.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"three-vessel view with color Doppler"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (2006), *Prenatal detection of heart defects in a non‐selected population of 30 149 fetuses—detection rates and outcome* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Reduced left heart growth on serial scans
 - **Modality**: fetal echocardiography | **Gestational Age**: Midtrimester with serial follow-up where available
- **Study Observation**: Serial left heart growth either tracked normal growth or was slower, sometimes producing progressive hypoplasia.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Growth of left heart structures in most of the fetuses either paralleled normal growth or was slower than normal"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [FINDING] Gallbladder left of umbilical vein
- **Indicates**: The gallbladder left of the umbilical vein is described as a primary indicator of abnormal situs.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"a gallbladder located to the left of the umbilical vein"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M Bronshtein et al. (2002), *Sonographic definition of the fetal situs* [Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Right arm of normal V
- **Normal Anatomy**: Aortic arch
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"right arm represents the aortic arch"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Achiron et al. (2002), *Anomalies of the fetal aortic arch: a novel sonographic approach to in‐utero diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Small TT-ratio in trisomy cohort
- **Study Definition**: TT-ratio below 2 SD under the normal-reference mean.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Small TT-ratio defined as TT-ratio < 2 SD below the mean"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: K. Karl et al. (2012), *Thymic–thoracic ratio in fetuses with trisomy 21, 18 or 13* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Low mitral-to-tricuspid orifice ratio
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography
- **Measurement**: Mitral orifice diameter divided by tricuspid orifice diameter, compared with GA reference.
- **Limitation**: Substantial false-positive overlap.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"measurements were expressed as a proportion of the expected mean for gestational age"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Gurleen K Sharland et al. (1994), *Coarctation of the aorta: difficulties in prenatal diagnosis.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Normal three-vessel linear order
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: Pulmonary artery, aorta, SVC line up from left anterior to right posterior.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"arranged in a straight line from the left anterior to the right posterior aspect ... decreasing order of their diameters"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S. ‐J. Yoo et al. (1997), *Three‐vessel view of the fetal upper mediastinum: an easy means of detecting abnormalities of the ventricular outflow tracts and great arteries during obstetric screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Association: Complex CHD with abdominal situs inversus
- **Source Observed Association**: Among total-population CHD cases with normal karyotype, Table 9 reports one critical case with complex chd and associated abdominal situs inversus.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Complex CHD  abdominal situs inversus  1"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Maternal adipose thickness has a nonlinear association with image acquisition
- **Direction Of Association**: Greater thickness reduced probability, nonlinearly
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the probability of imaging the heart decreased as the adipose tissue thickness increased."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1993), *Fetal echocardiography: factors that influence imaging of the fetal heart during the second trimester of pregnancy* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Right-sided abdominal aorta
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: 20 weeks in this case
- **Appearance**: Abdominal aorta on fetal right
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Transverse section through fetus’s upper abdomen demonstrates right-sided abdominal aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Julene S. Carvalho et al. (1997), *Situs Inversus With Complete Transposition in the Fetus* [Circulation]

### [FINDING] Expected Outflow tract views appearance in TOF/APV
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"TOF/APV 2 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Aorta arises from left ventricle
 - **Modality**: 2D ultrasound
- **Normal Anatomical Criterion**: Aortic outflow is observed leaving the left ventricle.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aortic outflow tract could be observed leaving the left ventricle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: G R DeVore et al. (1992), *The aortic and pulmonary outflow tract screening examination in the human fetus* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Main pulmonary artery diameter
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional echocardiography
- **Measurement Method**: midway between pulmonary valve and bifurcation during ventricular systole
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"main pulmonary artery diameter midway between the pulmonary valve and the bifurcation, also during ventricular systole"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [FINDING] Aortic valve opens freely
- **Criterion**: The aortic valve should move freely without thickened leaflets.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"aortic valve should move freely and should not be thickened"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Small VSD may be invisible on gray scale
 - **Modality**: fetal gray scale versus color Doppler
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Small defects were detected on color Doppler despite being invisible on gray-scale imaging
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Only small muscular septal defects not detectable on gray-scale echocardiography and those which were detected by flow across the septal wall during color Doppler mapping were included."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Outflow tract views appearance in Balanced AVC
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 1, 'meaning': 'normal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Balanced AVC 3 1"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Absent normal left V confluence
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Failure to see normal left arch/ductus V-shaped confluence may indicate an arch variant
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"does not form a ‘V’-shaped confluence with the ductus"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Levocardia apex direction with fetus face up
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal echocardiography
- **Cardiac Apex Screen Direction**: right
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Face Up Levocardia"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Timothy M. Cordes et al. (1994), *Distinguishing Right From Left: A Standardized Technique for Fetal Echocardiography* [Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Malalignment VSD (large)
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 1, 'meaning': 'normal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Malalignment VSD (large) 1 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Normal fetal ventricular septal axis
- **Normal Appearance**: The fetal heart is mainly in the left chest with ventricular septal axis about +40° from midline.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Normally the fetal heart is positioned primarily in the left chest with the ventricular septal axis 40 degrees from the midline."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: M M Abdullah et al. (2000), *Fetal cardiac dextroposition in the absence of an intrathoracic mass: sign of significant right lung hypoplasia.* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Normal pulmonary venous confluence
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Normal Appearance**: Two pulmonary veins converge into a venous sinus widely open to the left atrium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"confluence de 2 VP formant un sinus veineux pulmonaire largement ouvert dans l’OG"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: T. Hazelzet et al. (2015), *Retour veineux pulmonaire total isolé : y a-t-il des clés pour le dépistage prénatal ?* [Gynécologie Obstétrique & Fertilité]

### [FINDING] LVOT vessel does not bifurcate
- **Criterion**: The normal LVOT artery does not bifurcate near the heart.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"It does not bifurcate, indicating this to be the aorta"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Normal-cohort fluid depth measurement
 - **Modality**: 2D gray-scale or M-mode | **Gestational Age**: 19–38 weeks
- **Measurement Method**: Measure maximal fluid dimension with electronic caliper in M-mode; use gray-scale maximum if M-mode demonstration fails.
- **Observed Range**: 0.8–2.0 mm among gray-scale positive normal fetuses.
- **Study Cutoff**: More than 2 mm was excluded from this normal cohort.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"When it exceeded 2 mm, which is the upper limit of the normal value, we excluded the fetus from the study population."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2001), *Normal pericardial fluid in the fetus: color and spectral Doppler analysis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Aortic arch right of trachea
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Abnormal Position**: Right arch lies to the right of trachea on high transverse imaging
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"sausage-shaped aortic arch is located to the right of the trachea"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Aortic arch sidedness relative to trachea
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Definition**: Classify left/right arch by the trachea, not by where the aorta ascends
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"left- or right-sidedness of the aortic arch refers to the position of the aortic arch relative to the trachea"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] No normal retrotracheal crossing vessel
 - **Modality**: fetal ultrasound unless the evidence specifies a postnatal or schematic context
- **Normal Appearance**: No vessel crosses the midline behind trachea in the described normal axial planes
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"no vascular structure crossing the midline behind the trachea"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: S.‐J. Yoo et al. (2003), *Fetal sonographic diagnosis of aortic arch anomalies* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Color Doppler pulmonary venous drainage
- **Criterion**: In experienced hands, color or bidirectional power Doppler can show pulmonary venous drainage into the left atrium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"color or bidirectional power Doppler to visualize draining of these veins into LA"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Heart occupies one-third of thorax
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional ultrasound | **Gestational Age**: approximately 18 weeks
- **Expected Anatomy**: Heart occupies one-third of thorax
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"the heart occupying one-third of the thorax area"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: E. Tegnander et al. (1995), *Prenatal detection of heart defects at the routine fetal examination at 18 weeks in a non‐selected population* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Mitral stenosis
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 2, 'meaning': 'possibly abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Mitral stenosis 2 2"*

### [FINDING] Associated VSD and four-chamber visibility
- **Diagnostic Clue**: A VSD visible in the four-chamber view may prompt closer outflow tract examination and TGA recognition.

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in L-TGA
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"L-TGA 3 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

- **Measurement Rule**: Aortic arch and pulmonary trunk considered hypoplastic if vessel diameter was at least 3 SD below the normal mean for gestation.

- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. A. Hyett et al. (1997), *Increased nuchal translucency at 10—14 weeks of gestation as a marker for major cardiac defects* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Broad vertical arterial arm in illustrated HLHS

- **Abnormal Or Contextual Appearance**: The illustrated HLHS 3VTV has a broad vertical pulmonary/ductal arterial arm.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"broad arterial arm with a course parallel to the ultrasound beam"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Marcin Wiechec et al. (2015), *Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Defects at the 11‐ to 13‐Week Scan Using a Simple Color Doppler Protocol Including the 4‐Chamber and 3‐Vessel and Trachea Views* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Turbulent aortic forward flow
 - **Modality**: color Doppler
- **Appearance Or Interpretation**: Color Doppler may show turbulent increased-velocity forward flow across the aortic valve.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"In milder AS, doming and mild thickening of the aortic valve may be observed. Color and pulsed Doppler interrogation of the aortic outflow tract usually reveals increased velocities with minimal gradient and often mild post-stenotic dilation of the ascending aorta."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Yuka Yamamoto et al. (2012), *Progression of outflow tract obstruction in the fetus* [Early Human Development]

### [FINDING] Atria approximately equal
- **Criterion**: The right and left atria are normally similar in size.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Both atrial chambers normally appear similar in size"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Truncus arteriosus
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 1, 'meaning': 'normal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Truncus arteriosus 1 3"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Aorta from left ventricle
- **Criterion**: The LVOT vessel arises from the morphological left ventricle.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"great vessel originating from the morphological left ventricle"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Expected Four-chamber view appearance in Ebstein anomaly/TVD
- **Expected View Grade**: {'grade': 3, 'meaning': 'abnormal'}
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Ebstein anomaly/TVD 3 2"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Mark S. Sklansky et al. (2009), *Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Disease* [Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine]

### [FINDING] Transseptal color Doppler flow
 - **Modality**: color and pulsed-wave Doppler
- **Abnormal Appearance**: Color Doppler may show bidirectional flow across a septal defect
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Color Doppler echocardiography may demonstrate bidirectional flow across the area of defect"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: R. Axt‐Fliedner et al. (2006), *Isolated ventricular septal defects detected by color Doppler imaging: evolution during fetal and first year of postnatal life* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Foramen ovale flap in left atrium
- **Criterion**: The foramen ovale flap is seen moving within the left atrium.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"foramen ovale flap moves within the left atrium"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2023), *ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): fetal cardiac screening* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [FINDING] Ductus-plane aortic root appearance
 - **Modality**: two-dimensional fetal ultrasound
- **Criterion**: Aortic root is circular with aortic valve at center; right atrioventricular junction is visible.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"The aortic root is seen as a circle with the aortic valve closing at its centre and the right atrioventricular junction is well visualised."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lindsey D Allan et al. (1980), *Echocardiographic and anatomical correlates in the fetus.* [British Heart Journal]

### [FINDING] Brain injury severity scoring
 - **Modality**: neonatal brain MRI/diffusion tensor imaging
- **Measurement Definition**: Brain injury severity was scored 0 for no injury, 1 for minimal WMI or grade I/II IVH, 2 for stroke, and 3 for moderate/severe WMI, grade III IVH, or global hypoxic-ischemic injury.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"0 indicates no injury; 1, minimal white matter injury ... 2, stroke; and 3, moderate to severe white matter injury"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Shabnam Peyvandi et al. (2016), *Association of Prenatal Diagnosis of Critical Congenital Heart Disease With Postnatal Brain Development and the Risk of Brain Injury* [JAMA Pediatrics]

### [FINDING] Left ventricular end-diastolic long-axis dimension
 - **Modality**: fetal two-dimensional echocardiography
- **Measurement Method**: four-chamber view from AV-valve annular level to endocardial apex
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"end-diastolic left and right ventricular long-axis dimensions measured in a four-chamber view"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: Lisa K. Hornberger et al. (1995), *Left Heart Obstructive Lesions and Left Ventricular Growth in the Midtrimester Fetus* [Circulation]

### [MEDIA] Figure 2 panel b
 - **Modality**: continuous-wave Doppler | **Scan Caption**: Critical AS encountered in a mid trimester fetus. a) Early in gestation the left ventricle was hypertrophied and there was turbulent forward flow by color Doppler through the aortic valve. b) CW Doppler interrogation suggested the peak aortic valve gradient was 30–35 mm Hg. ### [MEDIA] Figure 3 panel left_4cv
 - **Modality**: fetal color Doppler ultrasound | **Scan Caption**: A case of hypoplastic left heart syndrome at 12 weeks. The 4-chamber view (left) shows a color stripe on the right side, which represents filling of the right ventricle. In the 3-vessel and trachea view (right), a broad arterial arm with a course parallel to the ultrasound beam (vertical course) is visible and represents a dilated pulmonary artery and ductus arteriosus. Although the 2 arms of the V sign can be seen, their sizes are severely unequal, and the flow within the aortic arch is abnormal, showing retrograde flow on the lower right side (retrograde filling toward a hypoplastic aortic arch from the ductus arteriosus), which is usually difficult to visualize on B-mode imaging without color mapping.

In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4-chamber view (1) typically shows normal-appearing anatomy, with 2 symmetric ventricles, a continuous ventricular septum, and insertion of the atrioventricular valves. On color mapping, 2 stripes are visualized, which represent normal filling of the cardiac chambers during diastole. In the 3-vessel and trachea view (3), color Doppler imaging shows only 1 vessel in an oblique fashion instead of 2. The image of a single vessel that takes a wide sweep on leaving the right ventricle should always raise the suspicion of transposition of the great arteries. The pulmonary artery is not visible in this plane due to the inferior and posterior relationships with the aorta in this condition. This factor is why the next step should be a subtle tilt backward toward the 4-chamber view to the level of the classic 3-vessel view (2). In this view, 2 separate arterial signals are shown, and 1 of these vessels (right, representing the aorta) is located more anteriorly.

In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4-chamber view (1) typically shows normal-appearing anatomy, with 2 symmetric ventricles, a continuous ventricular septum, and insertion of the atrioventricular valves. On color mapping, 2 stripes are visualized, which represent normal filling of the cardiac chambers during diastole. In the 3-vessel and trachea view (3), color Doppler imaging shows only 1 vessel in an oblique fashion instead of 2. The image of a single vessel that takes a wide sweep on leaving the right ventricle should always raise the suspicion of transposition of the great arteries. The pulmonary artery is not visible in this plane due to the inferior and posterior relationships with the aorta in this condition. This factor is why the next step should be a subtle tilt backward toward the 4-chamber view to the level of the classic 3-vessel view (2). In this view, 2 separate arterial signals are shown, and 1 of these vessels (right, representing the aorta) is located more anteriorly.

The two peaks of the diastolic flow coincide with the e- and a-waves of the blood flow through the atrioventricular valve. LA, left atrium; LV, left ventricle; RA, right atrium; RV, right ventricle.

In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4-chamber view (1) typically shows normal-appearing anatomy, with 2 symmetric ventricles, a continuous ventricular septum, and insertion of the atrioventricular valves. On color mapping, 2 stripes are visualized, which represent normal filling of the cardiac chambers during diastole. In the 3-vessel and trachea view (3), color Doppler imaging shows only 1 vessel in an oblique fashion instead of 2. The image of a single vessel that takes a wide sweep on leaving the right ventricle should always raise the suspicion of transposition of the great arteries. The pulmonary artery is not visible in this plane due to the inferior and posterior relationships with the aorta in this condition. This factor is why the next step should be a subtle tilt backward toward the 4-chamber view to the level of the classic 3-vessel view (2). In this view, 2 separate arterial signals are shown, and 1 of these vessels (right, representing the aorta) is located more anteriorly.

### [MEDIA] Figure 6 panel c
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography | **Scan Caption**: An example of the progressive nature of severe PS from the mid-trimester. In all images, the arrow points to RV apex. a) At 16 weeks, the four-chamber view demonstrated a dilated RV with poor systolic function. b) By 28 weeks there was mild to moderate RV hypoplasia and c) by term, the RV was very hypoplastic, with its functional cavity insufficient to sustain the pulmonary circulation. ### [MEDIA] Figure 4 panel 3
 - **Modality**: fetal color Doppler ultrasound | **Scan Caption**: D-Transposition of the great arteries at 12 weeks: 4-chamber view (4CV), 3-vessel view (3VV), and 3-vessel and trachea view (3VTV) of D-transposition of the great arteries (1–3) and a normal heart (4–6). In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4-chamber view (1) typically shows normal-appearing anatomy, with 2 symmetric ventricles, a continuous ventricular septum, and insertion of the atrioventricular valves. On color mapping, 2 stripes are visualized, which represent normal filling of the cardiac chambers during diastole. In the 3-vessel and trachea view (3), color Doppler imaging shows only 1 vessel in an oblique fashion instead of 2. The image of a single vessel that takes a wide sweep on leaving the right ventricle should always raise the suspicion of transposition of the great arteries. The pulmonary artery is not visible in this plane due to the inferior and posterior relationships with the aorta in this condition. This factor is why the next step should be a subtle tilt backward toward the 4-chamber view to the level of the classic 3-vessel view (2). In this view, 2 separate arterial signals are shown, and 1 of these vessels (right, representing the aorta) is located more anteriorly.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"D-Transposition of the great arteries at 12 weeks: 4-chamber view (4CV), 3-vessel view (3VV), and 3-vessel and trachea view (3VTV) of D-transposition of the great arteries (1–3) and a normal heart (4–6). In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4"*

### [MEDIA] Figure 4 panel e
 - **Modality**: continuous-wave Doppler | **Scan Caption**: Fetal echocardiographic images obtained in a 27 week fetus with critical AS, progressive mitral insufficiency and evolution of hydrops. a) A thickened, doming and hypoplastic aortic valve (arrow) and significant LV hypertrophy was demonstrated. Of note, the inflow Dopplers demonstrated in the same image show a dominant E wave during early ventricular filling with little A wave, the reverse of that observed in fetuses with progressive left heart hypoplasia and perhaps related to reduced left atrial function and differences in myocardial diastolic function. f) Pulmonary venous Dopplers are also quite different in the presence of a very dilated left atrium with little A wave reversal in atrial systole (arrows) and significant pulsatility despite atrial level restriction in this fetus. Ao, ascending aorta; LV, left ventricle; LA, left atrium; MR, mitral regurgitation; RV, right ventricle; E, early ventricular filling; A, atrial contraction.

### [MEDIA] Figure 5 panel left_upper
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound | **Scan Caption**: Figure 5 Maneuvers for visualization of the long-axis views of the aortic and ductal arches. For the aortic arch (AA), a three-vessel view is obtained so that the ascending aorta (A) and descending aorta (DA) are aligned vertically with the sonographic beam axis (left upper panel). Then the transducer is rotated 90◦ . The aortic arch is shown as a candy cane-shaped structure arising from the junction of the right (RA) and left (LA) atria (left lower panel). Note the head and neck branches of the aortic arch. For the ductal arch, a three-vessel view is obtained so that the main pulmonary artery (P) and descending aorta are aligned vertically with the sonographic beam axis (right upper panel). Then the transducer is rotated 90◦ . The ductal arch is shown as a hockey stick-shaped structure that is a continuation of the main pulmonary artery that arises from the right ventricle (RV). It does not give rise to any head and neck branches.

Extreme maternal obesity made the visualization of the ventriculo-arterial connection impossible on FFU (right); on THI (left) it was possible to detect the malalignment of the ventricular septal defect (VSD) with an overriding aorta. The arrowhead indicates the bright dot at the end of the VSD, which is distinguishable only on the THI frame. Ao, aorta; LV, left ventricle; RA, right atrium; SV, single ventricle.

### [MEDIA] Figure 5 panel right_upper
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound | **Scan Caption**: Figure 5 Maneuvers for visualization of the long-axis views of the aortic and ductal arches. For the aortic arch (AA), a three-vessel view is obtained so that the ascending aorta (A) and descending aorta (DA) are aligned vertically with the sonographic beam axis (left upper panel). Then the transducer is rotated 90◦ . The aortic arch is shown as a candy cane-shaped structure arising from the junction of the right (RA) and left (LA) atria (left lower panel). Note the head and neck branches of the aortic arch. For the ductal arch, a three-vessel view is obtained so that the main pulmonary artery (P) and descending aorta are aligned vertically with the sonographic beam axis (right upper panel). Then the transducer is rotated 90◦ . The ductal arch is shown as a hockey stick-shaped structure that is a continuation of the main pulmonary artery that arises from the right ventricle (RV). It does not give rise to any head and neck branches.

(a) Critical aortic stenosis at 33 weeks’ gestation. The inversion of the foramen ovale flap indicating reverse left-to-right shunt is readily evident only in the THI image (arrowhead). Also the right ventricle is barely visible in the THI image only (arrow). (b) Double-inlet single ventricle at 29 weeks’ gestation. The atrioventricular plane (arrows) and the redundant chordae tendinae of the two valves are evident in the THI but not in the FFU image. Also the ventricular wall is ill-defined in the latter image. (c) Mitral stenosis in Shone syndrome (mitral and aortic stenosis, aortic coarctation) at 28 weeks’ gestation. The hypertrophy of the right ventricle and the mitral stenosis can be better assessed in the THI image. (d) Tetralogy of Fallot in a fetus with trisomy 21 at 21 weeks’ gestation. Extreme maternal obesity made the visualization of the ventriculo-arterial connection impossible on FFU (right); on THI (left) it was possible to detect the malalignment of the ventricular septal defect (VSD) with an overriding aorta. The arrowhead indicates the bright dot at the end of the VSD, which is distinguishable only on the THI frame. Ao, aorta; LV, left ventricle; RA, right atrium; SV, single ventricle.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"Double-inlet single ventricle at 29 weeks’ gestation. The atrioventricular plane (arrows) and the redundant chordae tendinae of the two valves are evident in the THI but not in the FFU image."*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: D. Paladini et al. (2004), *The role of tissue harmonic imaging in fetal echocardiography* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

### [MEDIA] Figure 4 panel 6
 - **Modality**: fetal color Doppler ultrasound | **Scan Caption**: D-Transposition of the great arteries at 12 weeks: 4-chamber view (4CV), 3-vessel view (3VV), and 3-vessel and trachea view (3VTV) of D-transposition of the great arteries (1–3) and a normal heart (4–6). In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4-chamber view (1) typically shows normal-appearing anatomy, with 2 symmetric ventricles, a continuous ventricular septum, and insertion of the atrioventricular valves. On color mapping, 2 stripes are visualized, which represent normal filling of the cardiac chambers during diastole. In the 3-vessel and trachea view (3), color Doppler imaging shows only 1 vessel in an oblique fashion instead of 2. The image of a single vessel that takes a wide sweep on leaving the right ventricle should always raise the suspicion of transposition of the great arteries. The pulmonary artery is not visible in this plane due to the inferior and posterior relationships with the aorta in this condition. This factor is why the next step should be a subtle tilt backward toward the 4-chamber view to the level of the classic 3-vessel view (2). In this view, 2 separate arterial signals are shown, and 1 of these vessels (right, representing the aorta) is located more anteriorly.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"D-Transposition of the great arteries at 12 weeks: 4-chamber view (4CV), 3-vessel view (3VV), and 3-vessel and trachea view (3VTV) of D-transposition of the great arteries (1–3) and a normal heart (4–6). In isolated D-transposition of the great arteries, the 4"*

### [MEDIA] Figure 2 panel d
 - **Modality**: M-mode echocardiography | **Scan Caption**: Figure 2 M-mode images showing regular bradycardia (constant V-V intervals) with atrioventricular (AV) ratio > 1:1 (i.e. atrial rate greater than ventricular rate). Differential diagnosis is between pathological heart block (blocked sinus beat (B-SB)) and physiological block due to blocked ectopic beats (B-E). (a,b) AV block in the same 26-week fetus. Note that atrial contractions (A-A intervals) are regular. In (a) there is 2:1 AV block, seen by the constant AV interval preceding each ventricular contraction (oblique arrows show conducted beats). In (b) there is complete AV block, determined by the lack of time relationship between atrial (A) and ventricular (V) systoles. (c,d) Blocked bigeminy in two fetuses, at 21 weeks (c) and 17 weeks (d). Note that atrial contractions are regularly irregular. A short interval (A to B-E) alternates with a long interval (B-E to A). This is more obvious in (c) than in (d). The less obvious irregularity of the A-A interval in (d) (one shorter, one longer) can simulate 2:1 AV block. Each A is followed by a V with a constant A-V interval, indicating AV conduction of a normal sinus beat (oblique arrows). HR, fetal heart rate.
- **Clinical Evidence**: *"at 17 weeks (d) ... can simulate 2:1 AV block"*
- **Guideline / Reference Citation**: J. S. Carvalho et al. (2014), *Primary bradycardia: keys and pitfalls in diagnosis* [Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology]

There is a 3:2 AV ratio but, contrary to (b), the non-conducted beat corresponds to a B-E (physiological block). B-SB, blocked sinus beat.

### [MEDIA] Figure 5 panel left_lower
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal ultrasound | **Scan Caption**: Figure 5 Maneuvers for visualization of the long-axis views of the aortic and ductal arches. For the aortic arch (AA), a three-vessel view is obtained so that the ascending aorta (A) and descending aorta (DA) are aligned vertically with the sonographic beam axis (left upper panel). Then the transducer is rotated 90◦ . The aortic arch is shown as a candy cane-shaped structure arising from the junction of the right (RA) and left (LA) atria (left lower panel). Note the head and neck branches of the aortic arch. For the ductal arch, a three-vessel view is obtained so that the main pulmonary artery (P) and descending aorta are aligned vertically with the sonographic beam axis (right upper panel). Then the transducer is rotated 90◦ . The ductal arch is shown as a hockey stick-shaped structure that is a continuation of the main pulmonary artery that arises from the right ventricle (RV). It does not give rise to any head and neck branches.

### [MEDIA] Figure 2 panel c
 - **Modality**: 2D fetal echocardiography | **Scan Caption**: Critical AS encountered in a mid trimester fetus. a) Early in gestation the left ventricle was hypertrophied and there was turbulent forward flow by color Doppler through the aortic valve. b) CW Doppler interrogation suggested the peak aortic valve gradient was 30–35 mm Hg. A, flow in atrial systole; V, flow in ventricular systole; E, flow through the pulmonary veins in early ventricular diastole; LV, left ventricle; RA, right atrium; LA, left atrium; Ao, aorta; dAo, descending aorta.
